docs.title: 23.12.5. The [HtmlResponse] response
docs.text:
When the session type is [html], an object of type [HtmlResponse] is instantiated to send the response to the client. This object will send the client a HTML document, which depends on the status code returned by the secondary controller that processed the action. This mapping, [état => vue], is entered in the configuration file [config.json] as follows:

    "vues": {
        "vue-authentification.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "vue-calcul-impot.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "vue-liste-simulations.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "vue-erreurs": "vue-erreurs.php"

This configuration is interpreted as follows: [‘nom de la vue' => ‘états associés à cette vue']:

  • line 56: if the secondary controller returned a state from the [700, 221, 400] table, then display the [vue-authentification.php] view;
  • line 57: if the secondary controller returned a status from the [200, 300, 341, 350, 800] table, then display the [vue-calcul-impot.php] view;
  • Line 58: If the secondary controller returned a status from the [500, 600] table, then display the [vue-liste-simulations.php] view;
  • Line 60: If the secondary controller has returned a status that is not in any of the previous arrays, then display view [vue-erreurs.php].

The views are contained in the [Views] folder of the project. The code for the [HtmlResponse] class is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// a response HTML: one of the views in the folder [Views]
final class HtmlResponse extends ParentResponse
{
     #[\Override]
    public function send(
        Request $request,
        Session $session,
        array $config,
        int $statusCode,
        array $content,
        array $headers = [],
        ?Logger $logger = null
    ): void {
         // The response HTML depends on the status code returned by the controller
        $état = $content["état"];
         // Each status corresponds to a view: we look for the first view whose status list contains [$état]
         // If no view matches, it is an unexpected error: the error view is displayed
        $vue = array_find_key(
            $config["vues"],
            fn(array $états): bool => in_array($état, $états, true)
        ) ?? $config["vue-erreurs"];
         // The view is executed: what it outputs is placed in a buffer instead of being sent to the client
         // The view has access to the method’s variables [$request, $session, $config, $content]
        ob_start();
        require __DIR__ . "/../Views/$vue";
         // The contents of the buffer—the document HTML—are retrieved, and the buffer is cleared
        $html = ob_get_clean();
         // the parent class sends the response
        $this->sendResponse($statusCode, $html, "text/html", $headers);
         // Log the controller’s response in JSON, excluding HTML
        $this->log($logger, $content);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 26: The view to be displayed depends on the status code returned by the controller that processed the action. This code is in [$content["état"]];
  • Lines 29–32: The application configuration is searched for the view that corresponds to this status. The function [array_find_key] (PHP 8.4) returns the key of the first element in the array [$config["vues"]] that satisfies the condition expressed by the arrowed function—in this case, the name of the first view whose list of states contains [$état]. If no element satisfies the condition, it returns [null]: this indicates an abnormal status code for the application HTML, and the error view is displayed using the operator [??]. The script PHP 7 performed this search using a fifteen-line loop [while];
  • lines 35–38: the code PHP from the selected view is executed, and the result is stored in the variable [$html]. This code warrants some explanation. Let’s imagine that the selected view is [vue-authentification.php], which displays a web authentication form:
    • Line 35: The function [ob_start] initiates what the documentation refers to as an output delay. Anything written by the operations [print], [echo], or by the text HTML from an included script—and which would normally be sent immediately to the client—is placed in an output buffer (ob) without being sent to the client;
    • Line 36: The view [vue-authentification.php] is loaded; this is a dynamic view HTML containing code PHP. Two things then happen. First, the PHP code in the view is executed. The result is a page that contains only HTML, or even CSS and JavaScript, but no longer PHP. Next, this HTML code is normally sent to the client. This is actually the case for any text encountered by the PHP interpreter that is not PHP code. Due to the output delay, this code HTML is placed in the output buffer without being sent to the client;
    • Line 38: The [ob_get_clean] function does two things: it returns the contents of the output buffer—that is, the HTML page that was placed there—and it clears the buffer and stops the output delay. From the client’s perspective, it’s as if nothing had happened: it still hasn’t received anything;
  • The view is included by the [send] method: The view's code therefore has access to the method's local variables, specifically its parameters [$request], [$session], [$config], and [$content]. This is how the view receives the data it needs to display;
  • [__DIR__] is the absolute path to the folder containing the currently running script, in this case the [Responses] folder. To find the view, you must therefore go up one level to [..] and then enter the [Views] folder;
  • Line 40: The parent class sends the response to the client, with the type [text/html];
  • line 42: the response [$content] provided by the secondary controller that processed the current action is logged as JSON, without the HTML.

docs.title: 23.12.6. [curl] Tests
docs.text:
To truly test the session’s HTML mode, we would need to review all the views. We’ll do that later. For now, we’ll simply verify that a successful [init-session] action (status 700) in a new [html]-type session does indeed produce a HTML response. According to the configuration file, the view [vue-authentification.php] is the response:

> curl -D - -o vue.html -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html"
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:53 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate
Set-Cookie: PHPSESSID=60bf588b0873f085af3b33940c0d8417; path=/
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Connection: close
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
  • Line 1: The [-D -] option instructs [curl] to write the HTTP headers of the response to standard output (the [-] file), the [-o vue.html] option to write the body of the response to the [vue.html] file;
  • Line 11: The response is a HTML document.

When opened in a browser, the file [vue.html] displays the authentication view, which is shown below.

docs.title: 23.13.1. Overview of Views
docs.text:
The HTML web application uses four views. The authentication view:

The tax calculation view:

The simulation list view:

Unexpected Errors View:

The views use the CSS [Bootstrap] framework, version 5.3. Course PHP 7 used version 4.1: some classes CSS have changed or been removed; we’ll point these out as we go. We’ll describe these views one by one.

docs.title: 23.13.2.1. Overview of the View
docs.text:
The authentication view is as follows:

The view consists of three elements that we’ll call fragments:

  • the top banner, with the logo and title, is generated by the script [v-bandeau.php];
  • the authentication form is generated by the script [v-authentification.php];
  • the pink error box, displayed only when there are errors, is generated by the script [v-erreurs.php].

The authentication view is generated by the following page, [vue-authentification.php]:

<?php
// the authentication view—statuses [700, 221, 400]
// variables are inherited from the method [HtmlResponse::send], which performs the [require] for this view:
// Request $request: the current request
// Session $session: the application session
// array $config: the application configuration
// array $content: the controller response [action, état, réponse]

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// The view model is calculated
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
     // The model depends on the application's state
    return match ($content["état"]) {
         // Authentication failed: the entered username is displayed again along with an error message
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
            "erreurs" => ["Echec de l'authentification"],
        ],
         // 700, 400: empty form, no errors
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "erreurs" => []],
    };
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
     <!-- document encoded in UTF-8, displayed across the full width of the screen -->
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
     <!-- Bootstrap 5.3 -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
     <!-- header -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-bandeau.php" ?>
     <!-- 9-column authentication form -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-authentification.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- If there are errors, they are displayed below the form -->
    <?php if ($modèle->erreurs !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-erreurs.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • lines 2–7: The view is executed by the [require] statement in the [HtmlResponse::send] method. It inherits the variables from this method;
  • lines 13–28: The PHP section of the view calculates the view template. We’ll come back to this a little later;
  • line 30: a HTML5 document begins with this line;
  • lines 31–61: the HTML page is enclosed within the [<html>] and [</html>] tags. The [lang] attribute specifies the document’s language;
  • lines 32–40: header (head) of the HTML document:
    • line 34: the [<meta charset>] tag indicates that the document is encoded in UTF-8;
    • Line 35: The [<meta name="viewport">] tag sets the initial display of the view: across the full width of the screen displaying it (width) at its initial size (initial-scale). The value [shrink-to-fit=no] from version PHP 7 is no longer used with current browsers;
    • Lines 37–38: The [<link rel="stylesheet">] tag specifies the CSS file that governs the view’s appearance. We are using the CSS [Bootstrap] 5.3.8 framework, downloaded from the [jsDelivr] ([https://getbootstrap.com/docs/5.3/getting-started/introduction/]) distribution network. The [integrity] attribute contains the file’s fingerprint: the browser rejects the downloaded file if it does not match this fingerprint, which protects the page from file tampering on the distribution network;
    • line 39: the [<title>] tag sets the page title, which is displayed in the browser tab;
  • Lines 41–60: The body of the web page is enclosed within the [<body>] and [</body>] tags;
  • line 42: the [<div>] tag delimits a section of the displayed page. The [class] attributes used in the view all refer to the CSS Bootstrap framework. The [<div class="container">] tag delimits a Bootstrap container, centered on the page;
  • line 44: the [v-bandeau.php] fragment is included, which generates the page header. We’ll describe it shortly. The path is constructed using [__DIR__], the [Views] folder: a simple relative path such as ["v-bandeau.php"] would first be searched for in the directories specified by the [include_path] directive (PHP), then in the calling script’s folder ([Responses]) and the current folder, which can lead to unexpected results;
  • Lines 46–47: The [<div class="row">] tag delimits a Bootstrap row. These rows consist of 12 columns. The [<div class="col-md-9">] tag delimits a section of 9 columns;
  • line 48: the fragment [v-authentification.php] is included, which displays the authentication form;
  • lines 52–58: if the model’s error list is not empty, the fragment [v-erreurs.php] is included, which displays the errors in a new Bootstrap row. Here, we use the alternative syntax for control structures in PHP, [if (...):] ... [endif], which is more readable than curly braces in a HTML page. The PHP 7 script wrote the error code using the HTML syntax ([heredoc]) ([print <<<EOT ... EOT;]).

Let’s note the dynamic elements to be defined in this code:

  • [$modèle->erreurs]: the list of error messages, empty if there are no errors;
  • [$modèle->titreErreurs]: the text preceding the list of errors.

docs.title: 23.13.2.2. The fragment [v-bandeau.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-bandeau.php] displays the top banner on all views of the web application:

<?php
// fragment: the top banner for all views
// template: [$modèle->logo] (optional) — the URL of the logo, relative to the URL of the displayed page
?>
<!-- header: a light gray border with rounded corners -->
<div class="p-4 my-4 bg-body-tertiary rounded-3">
    <div class="row align-items-center">
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <img src="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg") ?>" alt="Cerisier en fleurs">
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-8">
            <h1>Calculez votre impôt</h1>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>

Comments

  • Line 6: The header is wrapped in a section whose Bootstrap classes provide inner spacing (p-4), vertical margins (my-4), a light gray background (bg-body-tertiary), and rounded corners (rounded-3). Course PHP 7 used the Bootstrap 4 class [jumbotron], which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5: these four classes replace it;
  • line 7: a Bootstrap row. The [align-items-center] class vertically centers the content of its columns;
  • lines 8–10: a [<img>] image is placed in the first four columns of the row;
  • line 9: the syntax [<?= expression ?>] is equivalent to [<?php echo expression ?>]. In other words, the value of the [src] attribute will be the value of the expression PHP. This is:
    • [$modèle->logo ?? "Views/logo.jpg"]: the URL of the logo, if the view template contains one; otherwise, the URL relative to [Views/logo.jpg]. All URL in the application are of the form [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=…]: the URL relative to [Views/logo.jpg] is supplemented by the browser with the path of the displayed page, resulting in [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/Views/logo.jpg]. The fragment PHP was used to construct the absolute URL of the logo from server variables ([REQUEST_SCHEME], [SERVER_NAME], [SERVER_PORT], [REQUEST_URI]) and a regular expression: this was unnecessary;
    • [htmlspecialchars(...)]: The function [htmlspecialchars] replaces the special characters in HTML with their entities: [&] becomes [&], [<] becomes [<], [>] becomes [>], ["] becomes ["], and ['] becomes [']. Thus, the value written to the page cannot break the [src] attribute or insert tags into the page;
  • Lines 11–13: The other 8 columns in the row (note that there are 12 in total) are used to display text in large font (tag [<h1>]).

Dynamic element: [$modèle->logo], the URL for the image displayed in the banner (optional).

Any dynamic value written to a HTML page must go through [htmlspecialchars]. This is the protection against XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) attacks: if a value entered by the user, or originating from an untrusted source, were written as-is into the page, a malicious user could inject code—such as [<script>…</script>]—which would be executed by the browsers of those viewing the page. Version 7 of PHP did not escape any values. Starting with version 8.1 of PHP, the default options for [htmlspecialchars] ([ENT_QUOTES | ENT_SUBSTITUTE | ENT_HTML401]) also encode the apostrophe: calling [htmlspecialchars($valeur)] is sufficient, whether the value is written in text or in an attribute delimited by quotation marks or apostrophes.

docs.title: 23.13.2.3. The fragment [v-authentification.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-authentification.php] displays the web application’s authentication form:

<?php
// element: the login form
// template: [$modèle->login] - the identifier to be displayed in the [user] input field
?>
<!-- form HTML - values are submitted using the action [authentifier-utilisateur] -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur">
     <!-- title on a blue background -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Veuillez vous authentifier</h4>
    </div>
     <!-- 1st line: ID -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
         <!-- text in 3 columns -->
        <label for="user" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">Nom d'utilisateur</label>
         <!-- text entry field in 4 columns -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="text" class="form-control" id="user" name="user"
                   placeholder="Nom d'utilisateur" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->login) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- 2nd line: password -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="password" class="col-md-3 col-form-label">Mot de passe</label>
         <!-- hidden text input field -->
        <div class="col-md-4">
            <input type="password" class="form-control" id="password" name="password"
                   placeholder="Mot de passe">
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- 3rd line: button of type [submit] -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-2">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Valider</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • Lines 6–36: The [<form>] tag delimits a HTML form. This form generally has the following characteristics:
    • It defines input fields ([<input>] tags);
    • it has a [submit]-type button that submits the entered values to the URL specified in the [action] attribute of the [<form>] tag. The HTTP method used to query this URL is specified in the [method] attribute of the [<form>] tag;
    • here, when the user clicks the [Valider] button, the browser will submit the values entered in the form to the URL and [main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur];
    • The posted values are the values entered by the user in the two input fields. They will be posted in the form [user=xx&password=yy]. The parameter names [user, password] correspond to the attributes [name] of the input fields;
  • lines 8–10: a Bootstrap section to display a title on a blue background;
  • lines 12–20: the first line of the form. The class [mb-3] adds a bottom margin to the line. Bootstrap 4 used the class [form-group], which no longer exists in Bootstrap 5;
  • Line 14: the label, in three columns. The [for] attribute of the [<label>] tag links the label to the [id] attribute of the input field: clicking on the label places the cursor in the input field;
  • line 16: the input field is placed within a four-column layout;
  • Lines 17–18: The HTML [<input>] tag defines an input field. It has several attributes:
    • [type="text"]: This is a text input field. You can type anything into it;
    • [class="form-control"]: Bootstrap style for the input field;
    • [id="user"]: ID of the input field. This ID is generally used by CSS and the code JavaScript;
    • [name="user"]: name of the input field. The value entered by the user will be submitted by the browser under this name ([user=xx]);
    • [placeholder="invite"]: the text displayed in the input field when the user has not yet typed anything;
    • [value="valeur"]: the text displayed in the input field as soon as it appears on the screen, before the user enters anything. This mechanism is used in the event of an error to display the input that caused the error. Here, this value will be the value of [$modèle->login], escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: an entered identifier containing a quotation mark cannot close the [value] attribute;
  • lines 22–29: similar code for the password entry field. The [type="password"] attribute creates a text input field where the characters being typed are hidden;
  • lines 31–35: a third line for the [Valider] button;
  • line 33: because it has the attribute [type="submit"], clicking this button triggers the browser to send the entered values to the server. The classes CSS and [btn btn-primary] display a blue button.

There is one last thing to explain. The [action="main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur"] attribute of the [<form>] tag defines an incomplete URL (it does not begin with http://machine:port/chemin). The authentication view will be obtained using various URL entries:

  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html];
  • [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur].

These URL files refer to a [main.php] document located at the path [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12]. This will be the case for all URL files in this application. The URL and [main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur] files will be prefixed with this path when the entered values are sent. These values will therefore be posted to the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=authentifier-utilisateur] files.

docs.title: 23.13.2.4. The [v-erreurs.php] fragment
docs.text:
The fragment [v-erreurs.php] displays a list of error messages. It is used by three of the application’s four views:

<?php
// snippet: a list of error messages in a pink box
// template: [$modèle->titreErreurs] - introductory text, [$modèle->erreurs] - error messages
?>
<div class="alert alert-danger" role="alert">
    <?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->titreErreurs) ?>
    <ul class="mb-0">
        <?php foreach ($modèle->erreurs as $erreur): ?>
            <li><?= htmlspecialchars($erreur) ?></li>
        <?php endforeach ?>
    </ul>
</div>
  • Line 5: Errors are displayed in a Bootstrap container with a pink background;
  • line 6: the text introducing the errors;
  • lines 7–11: the HTML [<ul>] tag (unordered list) displays a bulleted list. Each list item has the syntax [<li>élément</li>]. The class [mb-0] removes the bottom margin from the list;
  • Lines 8–10: the alternative syntax for the loop [foreach]. Each message is escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: controller error messages contain the values sent by the client ([valeur [x] invalide pour le paramètre [enfants]]). In course PHP 7, the view template contained the list HTML of errors, constructed by concatenating strings [<li>$erreur</li>]: A posted value containing code JavaScript would have been executed by the browser.

Dynamic elements: [$modèle->titreErreurs] and [$modèle->erreurs].

docs.title: 23.13.2.5. Visual testing
docs.text:
We can test the views well before integrating them into the application. The goal here is to test their visual appearance. We gather all the test views in the [Tests] folder of the project. To test the [vue-authentification.php] view, we need to create the data model it will display. The script [Tests/vue-authentification.php] is as follows:

<?php
// Visual test of the authentication view: the view is displayed using a test template

// the view template is calculated
$modèle = getModelForThisView();

function getModelForThisView(): stdClass
{
    return (object) [
         // user ID
        "login" => "albert",
         // error list—the second check ensures that special characters in HTML are neutralized
        "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
        "erreurs" => ["erreur1", "<b>erreur2</b>"],
         // the banner logo, related to the URL of this script
        "logo" => "../Views/logo.jpg",
    ];
}
?>
<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
     <!-- banner -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-bandeau.php" ?>
     <!-- 9-column authentication form -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-authentification.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- if there are errors, they are displayed below the form -->
    <?php if ($modèle->erreurs !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/../Views/v-erreurs.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

  • Line 5: The authentication view contains dynamic parts controlled by the [$modèle] object. This object is called the view template. According to one of the two definitions given for the acronym MVC, this is the M in MVC. It is calculated by the function [getModelForThisView]. A function defined at the top level of a script is known as soon as the script begins execution: it can be called before it is defined;
  • lines 9–17: The view model is an object of type [stdClass], the generic class of PHP. It is obtained here by converting an associative array into an object using the [(object)] operator: the array keys become the object’s attributes. The type [stdClass] is the only object type to which undeclared attributes can still be added (see the chapter on classes). An associative array could have been used instead to achieve the same result;
  • line 14: test values for the view’s dynamic elements. The second error contains HTML tags: we’ll verify that they are displayed as-is and not interpreted by the browser;
  • line 16: the URL for the logo is relative to the URL for the test script, located in the [Tests] folder;
  • line 32: the rest of the script is from the [Views/vue-authentification.php] view. The included fragments are those from the [Views] folder: these are the ones being tested. Course PHP 7 copied a version of them into the [Tests] folder.

The visual test is performed by requesting the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/Tests/vue-authentification.php] files in a browser:

Note that the [<b>] tag from the second error was displayed but not interpreted: the protection against XSS attacks is working. Continue these visual tests until you are satisfied with the result. During debugging, we modify the file in [VS Code] and then refresh the browser page (F5).

docs.title: 23.13.2.6. Calculating the View Model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, we can proceed to calculate the view model under real-world conditions. Let’s review the state codes that lead to this view. They can be found in the configuration file:

    "vues": {
        "vue-authentification.php": [700, 221, 400],
        "vue-calcul-impot.php": [200, 300, 341, 350, 800],
        "vue-liste-simulations.php": [500, 600]
    },
    "vue-erreurs": "vue-erreurs.php"

Therefore, the status codes [700, 221, 400] cause the authentication view to be displayed. To determine the meaning of these codes, we can refer to the [curl] tests performed on the JSON application:

  • 700 is the status code following a successful [init-session] action: the blank authentication form is then displayed;
  • 221 is the status code following a failed [authentifier-utilisateur] action (unrecognized credentials): the authentication form is then displayed so that the credentials can be corrected;
  • 400 is the status code following a successful [fin-session] action: the empty authentication form is then displayed.

Now that we know when the authentication form should be displayed, we can calculate its template in [vue-authentification.php]:

<?php
// the authentication view—statuses [700, 221, 400]
// Variables are inherited from the method [HtmlResponse::send], which performs the [require] for this view:
// Request $request: the current request
// Session $session: the application session
// array $config: the application configuration
// array $content: the controller's response [action, état, réponse]

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// The view template is calculated
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
     // The model depends on the application's state
    return match ($content["état"]) {
         // Authentication failed: the entered username is displayed again along with an error message
        221 => (object) [
            "login" => $request->request->getString("user"),
            "titreErreurs" => "Les erreurs suivantes se sont produites :",
            "erreurs" => ["Echec de l'authentification"],
        ],
         // 700, 400: empty form, no errors
        default => (object) ["login" => "", "erreurs" => []],
    };
}
?>

Comments

  • lines 3–7: We declare the variables inherited from the [HtmlResponse::send] method, which renders the view using [require];
  • line 10: the Symfony class used in the view code. The view has no namespace: without this statement, [Request] would refer to the class [\Request], which does not exist;
  • Lines 15–28: The [getModelForThisView] function calculates the view template. It receives the request and response from the controller—the only data it needs. The views do not have a [declare(strict_types=1)] declaration: they are HTML pages with some PHP code;
  • lines 18–27: The template depends on the status code returned by the controller that processed the current action:
    • lines 20–23: in the case of failed authentication: the username entered by the user, found in the posted parameters [$request->request], is redisplayed, and an error message is shown. The user can then try another authentication attempt;
    • line 26: status codes 700 and 400: a blank authentication form, with no errors.

Script PHP 7 used a statement that modified an object created at the beginning of the function.

docs.title: 23.13.2.8. Conclusion
docs.text:
We were able to test the view [vue-authentification.php] without having written the other views. This was possible because:

  • all the controllers have been written;
  • [curl] allows us to send requests to the server without needing the views. When writing controllers, you must be aware that anyone can do this. You must therefore be prepared to handle requests that no view would allow. These are created manually using [curl]. You should never assume a priori that “this request is impossible.” You must verify it.

docs.title: 23.13.3.1. Overview of the view
docs.text:
The tax calculation view is as follows:

The view has five parts:

  • the top banner is generated by the fragment [v-bandeau.php], which has already been presented;
  • the tax calculation form is generated by the fragment [v-calcul-impot.php];
  • a menu with two links is generated by the fragment [v-menu.php];
  • the calculation result is displayed in a green box;
  • Errors are displayed in a pink box by the fragment [v-erreurs.php].

The green and pink frames are never displayed together in the application: the screenshot above is from the visual test of the view, presented later. The tax calculation view is generated by the following script, [vue-calcul-impot.php], of which we are currently showing only the section HTML:

<!doctype html>
<html lang="fr">
<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.8/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
     <!-- header -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-bandeau.php" ?>
     <!-- two-column row: the menu spans 3 columns, the form spans 9 columns -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-3">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-menu.php" ?>
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-calcul-impot.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- success: the calculation result in a green frame, below the form -->
    <?php if ($modèle->résultats !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9 offset-md-3">
                <div class="alert alert-success" role="alert">
                    <?php foreach ($modèle->résultats as $ligne): ?>
                        <?= htmlspecialchars($ligne) ?><br>
                    <?php endforeach ?>
                </div>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
     <!-- failure: the error message in a pink box, below the form -->
    <?php if ($modèle->erreurs !== []): ?>
        <div class="row">
            <div class="col-md-9 offset-md-3">
                <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-erreurs.php" ?>
            </div>
        </div>
    <?php endif ?>
</div>
</body>
</html>

Comments

We will only comment on the new features:

  • line 57: inclusion of the top banner of the view;
  • lines 60–62: inclusion of the menu, which will occupy three columns of the Bootstrap row following the header;
  • lines 63–65: inclusion of the tax calculation form, which will occupy the remaining nine columns of this row;
  • lines 68–78: if the tax calculation was successful, the list [$modèle->résultats] is not empty, and the calculation result is displayed in a green frame (class [alert-success]). Each line of the result is followed by a line break ([<br>]). The box is on a new Bootstrap line and occupies nine columns offset by three columns (class [offset-md-3]). It will therefore appear immediately below the tax calculation form. Script PHP 7 achieved the offset using an empty column [<div class="col-md-3"></div>];
  • lines 80–86: if the tax calculation failed, the list [$modèle->erreurs] is not empty, and the errors are displayed in a pink box in the same location by the fragment [v-erreurs.php].

docs.title: 23.13.3.2. The fragment [v-calcul-impot.php]
docs.text:
The fragment [v-calcul-impot.php] displays the tax calculation form:

<?php
// snippet: the tax calculation form
// template: [$modèle->marié] (yes / no), [$modèle->enfants], [$modèle->salaire] - the displayed values
?>
<!-- form HTML posted with the action [calculer-impot] -->
<form method="post" action="main.php?action=calculer-impot">
     <!-- title on a blue background -->
    <div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
        <h4>Remplissez le formulaire ci-dessous puis validez-le</h4>
    </div>
     <!-- 1st line: marital status, two radio buttons in the same group [marié] -->
    <fieldset class="row mb-3">
        <legend class="col-form-label col-md-4 pt-0">Etes-vous marié(e) ou pacsé(e) ?</legend>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="marié" id="mariéOui" value="oui"
                    <?= $modèle->marié === "oui" ? "checked" : "" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="mariéOui">Oui</label>
            </div>
            <div class="form-check">
                <input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="marié" id="mariéNon" value="non"
                    <?= $modèle->marié === "oui" ? "" : "checked" ?>>
                <label class="form-check-label" for="mariéNon">Non</label>
            </div>
        </div>
    </fieldset>
     <!-- 2nd line: number of children, an integer >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="enfants" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Nombre d'enfants à charge</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="enfants" name="enfants"
                   placeholder="Nombre d'enfants à charge" value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->enfants) ?>">
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- 3rd line: annual salary, an integer >= 0 -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <label for="salaire" class="col-md-4 col-form-label">Salaire annuel</label>
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <input type="number" min="0" step="1" class="form-control" id="salaire" name="salaire"
                   placeholder="Salaire annuel" aria-describedby="salaireHelp"
                   value="<?= htmlspecialchars($modèle->salaire) ?>">
            <div id="salaireHelp" class="form-text">Arrondissez à l'euro inférieur</div>
        </div>
    </div>
     <!-- 4th row: button of type [submit] -->
    <div class="row mb-3">
        <div class="col-md-5">
            <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">Valider</button>
        </div>
    </div>
</form>

Comments

  • Line 6: The form HTML will be posted (attribute [method]) to URL and [main.php?action=calculer-impot] (attribute [action]). The posted values will be the values from the input fields:
    • the value of the selected radio button in the form [marié=oui] if the [Oui] radio button is selected, or [marié=non] if the [Non] radio button is selected. [marié] is the value of the [name] attribute for both radio buttons, [oui] and [non] are the values of their [value] attributes;
    • the value of the numeric input field [enfants] in the form [enfants=xx], where [xx] is the value entered by the user via the keyboard;
    • the value of the numeric input field [salaire] in the form [salaire=xx];
    • finally, the posted value will be in the form [marié=xx&enfants=yy&salaire=zz];
  • The entered values will be posted when the user clicks the button labeled [submit] on line 48;
  • Lines 12–26: the two radio buttons. The [<fieldset>] tag groups form elements together, and the [<legend>] tag provides them with a title;
  • lines 16–21: these are radio buttons because of the [type="radio"] attribute. The two radio buttons are part of the same radio button group because they share the same [name] attribute. The browser ensures that, within a group of radio buttons, only one is selected at any given time. Therefore, clicking one deselects the one that was previously selected;
  • lines 17–22: When the form is displayed, one of the radio buttons must be selected; to achieve this, simply add the [checked] attribute to the relevant [<input type="radio">] tag. The ternary operator sets this attribute on the [Oui] button if [$modèle->marié] equals [oui]; otherwise, it sets it on the [Non] button. Since the value being written is a constant, there is nothing to escape. Course PHP 7 inserted two variables, [checkedOui] and [checkedNon], into the template, containing the text [checked="checked"] or an empty string;
  • lines 31–32: a numeric input field ([type="number"]) with a minimum value of 0 ([min="0"]). In modern browsers, this means the user can only enter a number greater than or equal to 0. The input can also be made using a slider that can be clicked to increase or decrease the value. The attribute [step="1"] indicates that the slider operates in increments of 1: the slider will only accept integer values ranging from 0 to n in steps of 1. For manual entry, this means that numbers with decimals will not be accepted. In certain views, the children’s input field must be pre-filled with the last entry made in that field: this is the role of the attribute [value], whose value is provided by [$modèle->enfants];
  • Lines 39–42: The same explanations apply to salary entry as to those for children. The tooltip below the input field has the class [form-text]; Bootstrap 4 used the tag [<small>].

Dynamic elements: [$modèle->marié], [$modèle->enfants], [$modèle->salaire].

docs.title: 23.13.3.3. The [v-menu.php] snippet
docs.text:
This fragment displays a menu to the left of the tax calculation form. Its code is as follows:

<?php
// fragment: the application menu
// template: [$modèle->optionsMenu] - a table [texte du lien => URL cible]
?>
<!-- Bootstrap menu: a vertical list of links -->
<nav class="nav flex-column">
    <?php foreach ($modèle->optionsMenu as $texte => $url): ?>
        <a class="nav-link" href="<?= htmlspecialchars($url) ?>"><?= htmlspecialchars($texte) ?></a>
    <?php endforeach ?>
</nav>

Comments

  • Lines 6–10: The HTML and [<nav>] tags enclose a section of the document containing navigation links to other documents. The [nav, flex-column, nav-link] classes are Bootstrap classes that define the menu’s appearance: a vertical list of links;
  • line 7: the [$modèle->optionsMenu] template for the fragment is a table of the form [["Liste des simulations" => "main.php?action=lister-simulations", "Fin de session" => "main.php?action=fin-session"]];
  • line 8: the HTML [<a>] tag introduces a navigation link. [$url] is the URL that is navigated to when the [$texte] link is clicked. The browser then performs a [GET $url] operation. If [$url] is a relative URL, then it is supplemented by the path of the URL currently displayed by the browser. Thus, while the browser’s current URL is of type [http://chemin/main.php?paramètres], the [Liste des simulations] link leads to [http://chemin/main.php?action=lister-simulations]. The text and the URL are escaped by [htmlspecialchars]: in a URL, the character [&] that separates the parameters must be written as [&] in a HTML document.

docs.title: 23.13.3.5. Calculating the View Model
docs.text:
Once the visual appearance of the view has been determined, you can proceed to calculate the view model under real-world conditions. The status codes that lead to this view are the [200, 300, 341, 350, 800] codes in the configuration. To determine the meaning of these codes, you can refer to the [curl] tests performed on the JSON application:

  • 200 is the status code following a successful [authentifier-utilisateur] action: the blank tax calculation form is then displayed;
  • 300 is the status code following a successful [calculer-impot] action. The calculation form is then displayed with the data entered and the tax amount. The user can then perform another calculation;
  • 341 is the status code returned for a tax calculation with valid parameters when a lack of connection to SGBD causes an error;
  • 350 is the status code returned for a tax calculation with valid parameters when a failure to connect to the [Redis] server causes an error;
  • Status code 800 will be discussed later. We have not encountered it yet;
  • We assume here that the user is using a modern browser. Thus, with the form under consideration, it is not possible to enter negative numbers, non-numeric character strings, or decimal numbers in the [enfants, salaire] input fields. If these errors occur nonetheless (in a manually crafted request), they will be treated as unexpected errors: in that case, the view [vue-erreurs.php] will be displayed.

Now that we know when the tax calculation form should be displayed, we can define its template in [vue-calcul-impot.php]:

<?php
// tax calculation view - reports [200, 300, 341, 350, 800]
// inherits the variables [$request, $session, $config, $content] from the method [HtmlResponse::send]

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;

// The view template is calculated
$modèle = getModelForThisView($request, $content);

function getModelForThisView(Request $request, array $content): stdClass
{
    $modèle = new stdClass();
     // application status
    $état = $content["état"];
     // the form: empty (200, 800) or restored with the entered values (300, 341, 350)
    $saisie = in_array($état, [300, 341, 350], true);
    $modèle->marié = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("marié") : "non";
    $modèle->enfants = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("enfants") : "";
    $modèle->salaire = $saisie ? $request->request->getString("salaire") : "";
     // Calculation successful (300): the controller's response is an object [Simulation]
    $modèle->résultats = [];
    if ($état === 300) {
        $simulation = $content["réponse"];
        $modèle->résultats = [
            "Montant de l'impôt : $simulation->impôt euros",
            "Décôte : $simulation->décôte euros",
            "Réduction : $simulation->réduction euros",
            "Surcôte : $simulation->surcôte euros",
            "Taux d'imposition : " . $simulation->taux * 100 . " %",
        ];
    }
     // calculation failed (341: database unavailable, 350: Redis unavailable)
    $modèle->titreErreurs = "L'erreur suivante s'est produite :";
    $modèle->erreurs = in_array($état, [341, 350], true) ? [$content["réponse"]] : [];
     // the menu
    $modèle->optionsMenu = [
        "Liste des simulations" => "main.php?action=lister-simulations",
        "Fin de session" => "main.php?action=fin-session",
    ];
     // Rendering the template
    return $modèle;
}
?>

Comments

  • line 17: For reports 300, 341, and 350, the form is redisplayed with the entered values;
  • Lines 18–20: The entered values are found in the posted parameters [$request->request]. For reports 200 and 800, the form is empty, with the [Non] button checked;
  • Lines 23–32: Successful tax calculation. The response from the [$content["réponse"]] controller is a [Simulation] object: the result lines are constructed based on its attributes. The rate is displayed as a percentage. Since a simulation is an object, [$simulation->impôt] is interpolated directly into a string enclosed in quotation marks;
  • line 35: case where the tax calculation fails due to the database or server being unavailable ([Redis]). The controller’s response is then the error message;
  • Lines 37–40: the two menu options.

The view displaying the list of simulations is as follows:

The HTML section of the [vue-liste-simulations.php] script is as follows:

          integrity="sha384-sRIl4kxILFvY47J16cr9ZwB07vP4J8+LH7qKQnuqkuIAvNWLzeN8tE5YBujZqJLB" crossorigin="anonymous">
    <title>Application impots</title>
</head>
<body>
<div class="container">
     <!-- banner -->
    <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-bandeau.php" ?>
     <!-- two-column row: the menu across 3 columns, the simulations across 9 columns -->
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col-md-3">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-menu.php" ?>
        </div>
        <div class="col-md-9">
            <?php require __DIR__ . "/v-liste-simulations.php" ?>
        </div>
    </div>
</div>
</body>

  • Line 33: inclusion of the application banner;
  • line 37: inclusion of the menu. It will be displayed in three columns below the banner;
  • line 40: inclusion of the simulation table. It will be displayed in nine columns below the banner and to the right of the menu.

The fragment [v-liste-simulations.php] is as follows:

<?php
// snippet: the simulation table
// template: [$modèle->simulations] - the list of objects [Simulation] to display
?>
<!-- title on a blue background -->
<div class="alert alert-primary" role="alert">
    <h4>Liste de vos simulations</h4>
</div>
<!-- simulation table -->
<table class="table table-sm table-hover table-striped">
     <!-- headers for the ten columns in the table -->
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th scope="col">#</th>
        <th scope="col">Marié</th>
        <th scope="col">Nombre d'enfants</th>
        <th scope="col">Salaire annuel</th>
        <th scope="col">Montant impôt</th>
        <th scope="col">Surcôte</th>
        <th scope="col">Décôte</th>
        <th scope="col">Réduction</th>
        <th scope="col">Taux</th>
        <th scope="col"></th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
     <!-- table body: one row per simulation -->
    <tbody>
    <?php foreach ($modèle->simulations as $i => $simulation): ?>
        <tr>
             <!-- The simulation number is the row header -->
            <th scope="row"><?= $i ?></th>
            <td><?= htmlspecialchars($simulation->marié) ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->enfants ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->salaire ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->impôt ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->surcôte ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->décôte ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->réduction ?></td>
            <td><?= $simulation->taux ?></td>
             <!-- link to delete simulation No. $i -->
            <td><a href="<?= htmlspecialchars("main.php?action=supprimer-simulation&numéro=$i") ?>">Supprimer</a></td>
        </tr>
    <?php endforeach ?>
    </tbody>
</table>

Comments

  • Lines 10–45: A table named HTML is created using the [<table>] tag. Bootstrap classes give it a compact appearance (table-sm), a highlighted row when the mouse hovers over it (table-hover), and alternating row colors (table-striped);
  • Lines 12–25: The table column headers are defined within a ***[<thead>]*** (table head) tag. The ***[<tr>] (table row) tag defines a row. The [<th>] tag (table header) defines a column header. There are ten of them. [scope="col"] indicates that the header applies to the column. [scope="row"]* indicates that the header applies to the row;
  • lines 27–44: the [<tbody>] tag encloses the data displayed by the table;
  • line 28: the list of simulations is found in the [$modèle->simulations] template. It is a list of [Simulation] objects: [$i] is the simulation number in the list;
  • Lines 29–42: The [<tr>] tag encloses a row of the table;
  • line 31: the [<th scope="row">] tag defines the row header, the simulation number;
  • lines 32–39: each [<td>] tag defines a column in the row. Only the marital status—a string of characters—is escaped: the other attributes of the simulation are numbers, typed as such in the [Simulation] class, which cannot contain special characters from the HTML class;
  • Line 41: a link to delete the simulation. The URL [main.php?action=supprimer-simulation&numéro=$i] takes the number displayed in the first column of the table. The browser handles encoding the [é] character in the parameter name.

The status codes that lead to the simulation view are the [500, 600] codes in the configuration:

The script PHP 7 converted each object into an associative array using the getters of the class [Simulation]: with public attributes, this is unnecessary;

docs.title: 23.13.5. Viewing Unexpected Errors
docs.text:
Here, an unexpected error is defined as an error that should not have occurred during normal use of the web application. Let’s take the following request as an example, in session JSON:

> curl -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=calculer-impot" -d "salaire=y"
{"action":"calculer-impot","état":337,"réponse":["paramètre [marié] manquant","paramètre [enfants] manquant","valeur [y] invalide pour le paramètre [salaire]"]}

The parameters [marié] and [enfants] are missing, and the parameter [salaire] is invalid. However, in the HTML form of the web application, this situation cannot occur:

  • all parameters are present;
  • the parameter [marié], which derives its value from the [value] attributes of two radio buttons, must be either [oui] or [non];
  • with a modern browser, the [<input type="number" min="0" step="1" …>] attributes ensure that the entries for children and salary are necessarily integers >= 0.

However, nothing prevents a user from sending such a request to our server—using [curl] or their browser’s developer tools—during a HTML session. We’ll call an “unexpected error” any error that shouldn’t occur within the HTML application. If it does occur, it’s likely because someone is trying to “hack” the application. For educational purposes, we’ve decided to display an error page for these cases. In reality, we could re-display the last page sent to the client. To do this, we simply need to store the last HTML response sent in the session. In the event of an unexpected error, we return this response. This way, the user will have the impression that the server is not responding to their errors since the displayed page does not change.

docs.title: 23.13.6. Implementing Application Menu Actions
docs.text:
Here, we will discuss the implementation of menu actions. Let’s review the meanings of the links we’ve encountered:

ViewLinkTargetRoleTax Calculation[Liste des simulations][main.php?action=lister-simulations]Request a list of simulationsTax Calculation[Fin de session][main.php?action=fin-session]Request to end the sessionList of simulations[Calcul de l'impôt][main.php?action=afficher-calcul-impot]Display the tax calculation viewList of simulations[Fin de session][main.php?action=fin-session]Request to end the sessionUnexpected errors[Calcul de l'impôt][main.php?action=afficher-calcul-impot]Display the tax calculation viewUnexpected errors[Liste des simulations][main.php?action=lister-simulations]Request a list of simulationsUnexpected errors[Fin de session][main.php?action=fin-session]Request to end the session

Note that clicking a link triggers a GET to the link’s target. The [lister-simulations, fin-session] actions have been implemented using a GET operation, which allows us to use them as link targets. When the action is performed via a POST, using a link is no longer possible unless it is combined with a JavaScript.

From the actions listed above, it appears that the [afficher-calcul-impot] action has not yet been implemented. This is a navigation operation between two views: the JSON or XML server has no reason to implement it because it does not have the concept of a view. It is the HTML server that introduces this concept. We therefore need to implement the action [afficher-calcul-impot]. This will allow us to review the procedure for implementing an action within the server:

  • we add a case to the [Action] enumeration: [case AfficherCalculImpot = "afficher-calcul-impot";];
  • we write the secondary controller [AfficherCalculImpotController] to the [Controllers] folder;
  • add its file to the [dependencies] key in the [config.json] file;
  • add the branch [Action::AfficherCalculImpot => new AfficherCalculImpotController()] to the expression [match] of the main controller;
  • associate the status code returned by the controller, 800, with the tax calculation view in key [vues] of [config.json].

The [AfficherCalculImpotController] controller is as follows:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Session\Session;

// Action [afficher-calcul-impot]: Navigate to the tax calculation view (application HTML)
final class AfficherCalculImpotController implements InterfaceController
{
     #[\Override]
    public function execute(array $config, Request $request, Session $session): ControllerResult
    {
         // view change: simply return the status code associated with the target view
        return new ControllerResult(Response::HTTP_OK, 800, "");
    }
}
  • Line 14: Like the other secondary controllers, the new controller implements the [InterfaceController] interface;
  • line 20: View changes are easy to implement: simply set the state code associated with the target view—in this case, code 800. A view change cannot result in an error.

docs.title: 23.13.7. Real-World Testing
docs.text:
The code has been written, and each action has been tested with [curl]. We still need to test the view flow in a real-world scenario. We need a way to initialize the HTML session. We know that we need to send the parameters [action=init-session&type=html] to the server. To avoid having to type them into the browser’s address bar, we’ll add the script [index.php] to our application:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// redirect (code 302) to [main.php] in [html] mode
header("Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html");
  • Line 6: [header] is a function that adds a HTTP header to the response. The HTTP [Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html] header instructs the client browser to redirect to the specified URL. PHP then sets the response status to [302 Found].

The [index.php] script is requested along with the URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/index.php] scripts. When the client browser receives the redirect to the relative URL from [main.php?action=init-session&type=html], it will request the absolute URL for [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/main.php?action=init-session&type=html], and the HTML session will begin.

The startup URL can be simplified to [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/]. If no document is specified in URL, [Apache] uses the [index.html] or [index.php] document from the folder. In this case, the script [index.php] will therefore be used. Let’s verify this with [curl]:

> curl -i http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-12/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:51:53 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11

docs.title: 23.14.1. Client/server architecture
docs.text:
We will now focus on the client JSON [A] of the web service [B]. The client [A], like the web service [B], has a layered structure:

This architecture is reflected in the following code organization within the [scripts-console/impots/version-12] folder:

scripts-console/impots/version-12
├── Dao
│   ├── ClientDao.php
│   └── InterfaceClientDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── config.json
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── results.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Main
│   └── main.php
├── Metier
│   ├── ClientMetier.php
│   └── InterfaceClientMetier.php
└── Tests
    └── ClientMetierTest.php

The other classes used by the client have already been discussed and explained. As with previous clients, they are loaded from the folders where they were written:

ClassRole and OriginExceptionImpotsThe application's exception class. Version 5, folder [Entities]TaxPayerDataA taxpayer's data [marié, enfants, salaire]. Version 5, file [Entities]UtilitiesReading and writing files JSON. Version 5, folder [Utilities]TraitDaoImplementation of methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults]. Version 5, folder [Dao]SimulationA tax calculation simulation. Version 12 server, folder [Entities]

The client uses the server’s class [Simulation]: this is the format in which the server sends its simulations, and this class [readonly] with public attributes is suitable for both the client and the server. The class PHP 7 [BaseEntity], from which the client class [Simulation] 7 PHP was derived, no longer exists.

docs.title: 23.14.2.1. Interface
docs.text:
The interface of layer [dao] is as follows: [Dao/InterfaceClientDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the interface of the [dao] layer of the JSON web service client, version 12
// All methods throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception in case of an error
interface InterfaceClientDao
{
     // reads taxpayer data (implemented by the [TraitDao] process)
     /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

     // Save results (implemented by the trait [TraitDao])
     /** @param Simulation[] $simulations */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void;

     // [init-session] action: start of a JSON, XML, or HTML session
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void;

     // action [authentifier-utilisateur]
    public function authentifierUtilisateur(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void;

     // action [calculer-impot]: calculation of a taxpayer's tax
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): Simulation;

     // action [lister-simulations]: list of simulations for the session
     /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function listerSimulations(): array;

     // action [supprimer-simulation]: returns the new list of simulations
     /** @return Simulation[] */
    public function supprimerSimulation(int $numéro): array;

     // action [fin-session]
    public function finSession(): void;
}

Comments

  • Line 14: The [getTaxPayersData] method is used to process the JSON file containing taxpayer data. This method is implemented by the [TraitDao] feature in version 5;
  • Line 18: The [saveResults] method allows you to save the results of multiple tax calculations to a JSON file. Here as well, this method is implemented by the trait [TraitDao]. This trait delegates the work to the method [Utilitaires::écrireFichierJson], which can convert any object into JSON based on its public attributes: [TaxPayerData] objects in previous versions, [Simulation] objects here;
  • lines 21–38: a method has been created for each of the actions accepted by the web service, with the exception of the [afficher-calcul-impot] action, which is used only by the HTML application;
  • line 24: the [SensitiveParameter] attribute (PHP 8.2), which we’ve already encountered: if an exception is thrown while the method is executing, the password value will not appear in the call trace;
  • the documentation comments (PHPDoc), [@return Simulation[]], and [@param Simulation[] $simulations] specify the contents of the arrays. PHP cannot determine the type of an array’s contents: the type [array] does not specify that the elements are [Simulation] objects. These comments convey this information to the [VS Code] editor (PHP Intelephense extension), which can then suggest the attributes of [Simulation] when traversing the array.

docs.title: 23.14.2.2. Implémentation
docs.text:
The [InterfaceClientDao] interface is implemented by the following [ClientDao] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpClient\HttpClient;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\Exception\TransportExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\ResponseInterface;

// the [dao] client layer of the JSON web service, version 12
// one method per server action; the session is maintained using the session cookie
class ClientDao implements InterfaceClientDao
{
     // the version 5 trait implements the methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] of the interface
    use TraitDao;

     // the HTTP client
    private readonly HttpClientInterface $httpClient;
     // the session cookie (null until the server sends it)
    private ?string $sessionCookie = null;

     // constructor
     // $urlServer: the URL of the web service JSON
     // $httpClientOptions: options for the HTTP client (verify_peer, verify_host...)
     // $verbose: When set to true, server responses are displayed on the console
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $urlServer,
        array $httpClientOptions = [],
        private readonly bool $verbose = true,
    ) {
        $this->httpClient = HttpClient::create($httpClientOptions);
    }

Comments

  • Line 19: The class uses the [TraitDao] trait, which implements two methods of the interface:
    • [getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array];
    • [saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $simulations): void];
  • Line 22: The Symfony client HTTP is created only once, by the constructor, and is used for all requests. The client PHP used to create a new client HTTP in each method;
  • line 24: the session cookie. Its role was described with the client in version 9. It is set to [null] until the server sends it;
  • Lines 30–34: The constructor receives three parameters, two of which are promoted to attributes:
    • the URL and [$urlServer] from the JSON web service;
    • the [$httpClientOptions] options from the HTTP client. These come from the configuration file: as with version 11, these are the [verify_peer] and [verify_host] options, which would allow working with the self-signed certificate [Laragon] if the server’s URL used the schema [https];
    • a Boolean [$verbose] which, when set to [true], indicates that the class should display the server's responses on the console.

docs.title: The [initSession] method
docs.text:
The [initSession] method is implemented as follows:

     // action [init-session]: this must be the first action requested from the server
     #[\Override]
    public function initSession(string $type = "json"): void
    {
         // GET main.php?action=init-session&type=json - the response is a simple message
        $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "init-session", "type" => $type]);
    }

Since action [init-session] is the first action requested from the web service, method [initSession] will be the first method in the [dao] layer to be called.

Comments

  • Line 40: The desired session type is passed as a parameter. If no parameter is provided, a JSON session will be started. A JSON client can request a XML session: it will receive XML responses from version 11, which it will not be able to process;
  • Line 43: A GET request is sent to the web service. Its two parameters are placed in the URL: [main.php?action=init-session&type=json]. The server’s response (a simple message) is not processed. The private method [sendRequest] throws an exception if the response code HTTP is not 200 OK.

The client PHP 7 repeated the following steps in each of its methods: creating the client HTTP, preparing the request options (including the session cookie), and calling the method [getResponse]. We factored this work into the private method [sendRequest].

docs.title: The [sendRequest] method
docs.text:
// Sending a request to the server and processing its response
     // $method: GET or POST
     // $query: the parameters of URL
     // $body: the posted parameters (POST only)
     // returns the element [réponse] from the server's response JSON
    private function sendRequest(string $method, array $query, array $body = []): mixed
    {
         // the request options
        $options = ["query" => $query];
        if ($body !== []) {
             // the posted parameters are sent in the form [param1=v1&param2=v2...]
            $options["body"] = $body;
        }
        if ($this->sessionCookie !== null) {
             // The session cookie sent to us by the server is returned to the server
            $options["headers"] = ["Cookie" => $this->sessionCookie];
        }
         // We make the request—the response will only actually be read by [getResponse]
        $response = $this->httpClient->request($method, $this->urlServer, $options);
         // we process the response
        return $this->getResponse($response);
    }

Comments

  • line 51: the method receives the HTTP method from the request (GET or POST), the parameters from URL, and, for POST, the posted parameters. The [$body] parameter is optional; its default value is an empty array;
  • line 54: the [query] option of the Symfony client HTTP contains the parameters from URL. Symfony encodes them itself (the [numéro] parameter of the [supprimer-simulation] action contains an accented character);
  • line 57: when the [body] option is an array, Symfony sends the posted parameters in the form [param1=v1&param2=v2…] with the header [Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded], just as a browser does when posting a form;
  • lines 59–61: Starting with the second request, we send the session cookie back to the server that it sent to us. This is how the server retrieves the client’s session;
  • line 64: the request is prepared. Symfony’s HTTP client is asynchronous: the request is actually sent and the response read when we request the status, headers, or content of the response, which is what the [getResponse] method does;
  • line 66: the [réponse] element of the server’s response is returned.

docs.title: The [getResponse] method
docs.text:
The [getResponse] method is responsible for processing the web service response:

     // Processing the server's response
     // returns the element [réponse] from the response JSON {"action": ..., "status": ..., "response": ...}
    private function getResponse(ResponseInterface $response): mixed
    {
        try {
             // the status, headers, and JSON document from the response, even in the event of an error (false parameter)
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
            $headers = $response->getHeaders(false);
            $json = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (TransportExceptionInterface $ex) {
             // The server could not be reached
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur de communication avec le serveur ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
         // logs
        if ($this->verbose) {
            print "$json\n";
        }
         // the session cookie: we keep the last one sent by the server
         // (the action [fin-session] deletes the old cookie and sends a new one)
        foreach ($headers["set-cookie"] ?? [] as $cookie) {
            if (preg_match('/^PHPSESSID=([^;]+)/', $cookie, $champs) === 1) {
                $this->sessionCookie = "PHPSESSID=$champs[1]";
            }
        }
         // decoding the response JSON
        try {
            $array = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException) {
            $array = null;
        }
        if (!is_array($array) || !array_key_exists("réponse", $array)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Réponse du serveur invalide [$json]", 41);
        }
         // error?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
             // The exception message is the server's response supplemented by its status HTTP
            $message = json_encode(
                ["statut HTTP" => $statusCode] + $array,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new ExceptionImpots($message, 42);
        }
         // Extracting the useful part of the response
        return $array["réponse"];
    }

Comments

  • Line 71: The method is private. Its parameter is of type [ResponseInterface], the interface implemented by all responses from the Symfony client HTTP. Client PHP 7 used the type [CurlResponse], the response class when client HTTP is implemented with library [curl]: the [dao] layer was unnecessarily dependent on the implementation chosen by Symfony;
  • Lines 73–80: The response status, headers, and content are retrieved. The [false] parameter prevents Symfony from throwing an exception when the response status HTTP falls within the ranges [3xx, 4xx, 5xx]. If the server cannot be reached, Symfony throws a [TransportExceptionInterface] exception, which is converted to a [ExceptionImpots] exception with status code 40, as in previous versions;
  • lines 83–84: if in [$verbose] mode, the server’s response is displayed on the console;
  • lines 88–90: We retrieve the session cookie. Client PHP 7 only did this in the [initSession] method. We do this after every request because the server in version 12 changes the session cookie during the [fin-session] action: it sends two headers, the first to delete the old cookie ([PHPSESSID=deleted]) and the second for the new one. The loop retains the last one. The regular expression [/^PHPSESSID=([^;]+)/] captures the cookie’s value up to the first semicolon, which separates the value from the cookie’s attributes (path, expires, etc.);
  • line 95: the string JSON is parsed into an array. The option [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] causes a [JsonException] exception to be thrown if the string is not a valid JSON;
  • lines 99–100: If the response is not a JSON object with the key [réponse], it is not a response from our web service. A code 41 exception is thrown;
  • Lines 103–109: If the status of the server’s response HTTP is not 200, an exception with code 42 is thrown; the exception message is the server’s response JSON, supplemented by the status HTTP, as with the previous clients. The [+] operator, when applied to two associative arrays, merges them: the [["statut HTTP" => $statusCode]] array is populated with the keys [action, état, réponse] from the [$array] array;
  • Line 112: The relevant information is in [$array["réponse"]]. Depending on the action, this is a message, an associative array (a simulation), or a list of associative arrays (simulations). The method’s return type is therefore [mixed].

docs.title: The [authentifierUtilisateur] method
docs.text:
The [authentifierUtilisateur] method is as follows:

     // action [authentifier-utilisateur]
     #[\Override]
    public function authentifierUtilisateur(string $user, #[\SensitiveParameter] string $password): void
    {
         // POST main.php?action=authenticate-user with the posted parameters [user, password]
        $this->sendRequest(
            "POST",
            ["action" => "authentifier-utilisateur"],
            ["user" => $user, "password" => $password]
        );
    }

Comments

  • line 121: the client’s request is a POST;
  • line 122: the single parameter of the URL;
  • line 123: the parameters of the POST;
  • The response is not processed: we know that in the event of an error (HTTP code other than 200), the [getResponse] method itself throws an exception.

docs.title: The [calculerImpot] method
docs.text:
// action [calculer-impot]
     #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): Simulation
    {
         // POST main.php?action=calculate-tax with the posted parameters [marié, enfants, salaire]
        $réponse = $this->sendRequest(
            "POST",
            ["action" => "calculer-impot"],
            ["marié" => $marié, "enfants" => $enfants, "salaire" => $salaire]
        );
         // The response is the attribute table for a simulation
        return self::toSimulation($réponse);
    }

Comments

  • line 134: the single parameter of URL;
  • line 135: the three parameters of POST;
  • line 138: if you reach this point, it means that the [getResponse] method did not throw an exception. The response is the associative array of a simulation’s attributes. The [toSimulation] method, described a little further on, converts it into a [Simulation] object.

docs.title: The [listerSimulations] method
docs.text:
// action [lister-simulations]
     #[\Override]
    public function listerSimulations(): array
    {
         // GET main.php?action=list-simulations
        $réponse = $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "lister-simulations"]);
         // The response is a list of simulations
        return self::getSimulations($réponse);
    }

Comments

  • line 146: a GET request with the single parameter [action];
  • line 148: the transformation of the response into a list of [Simulation] objects is handled by the private method [getSimulations].

docs.title: The [getSimulations] method
docs.text:
// converts the list of associative arrays received from the server into a list of objects [Simulation]
     /** @return Simulation[] */
    private static function getSimulations(array $réponse): array
    {
        return array_map(self::toSimulation(...), $réponse);
    }

     // converts an associative array [marié, enfants, salaire, impôt, ...] into an object [Simulation]
    private static function toSimulation(array $attributs): Simulation
    {
         // the array keys are the names of the constructor parameters of [Simulation]
        return new Simulation(...$attributs);
    }

Comments

  • line 153: the method receives the response from the server, a list of associative arrays, each containing all the attributes of a simulation. It does not use any object attributes: it is static and called by [self::getSimulations(...)];
  • line 155: the function [array_map] applies the method [toSimulation] to each element of the list and returns the list of results. The syntax [self::toSimulation(...)] (PHP 8.1, “first-class callable syntax”) creates an anonymous function (a [Closure]) from the method [toSimulation]. It replaces the old syntax [[self::class, "toSimulation"]];
  • line 162: the [...] operator unpacks the [$attributs] array into constructor arguments. Starting with PHP 8.1, the string keys of the array become named arguments: the key [marié] is passed to parameter [$marié], the key [impôt] to parameter [$impôt], and so on, regardless of the order of the keys in the array. If the server sent a key unknown to the constructor, PHP would throw a [Error] error;
  • the client PHP 7 used the method [setFromArrayOfAttributes] of the class [BaseEntity] to initialize the object [Simulation] with the elements of the array. Note that the JSON serialization of its [Simulation] objects contained the redundant attribute [arrayOfAttributes] inherited from the [BaseEntity] class. This is no longer the case.

docs.title: The [supprimerSimulation] method
docs.text:
// action [supprimer-simulation]
     #[\Override]
    public function supprimerSimulation(int $numéro): array
    {
         // GET main.php?action=delete-simulation&number=1
        $réponse = $this->sendRequest("GET", ["action" => "supprimer-simulation", "numéro" => $numéro]);
         // The server returns the new list of simulations
