  • lines 13–20: the logo is served (type [image/jpeg]).

Finally, the application’s URL is redirected to the [public] folder, whose [index.php] script in turn redirects to the main controller:

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/web-scripts/taxes/version-13/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Location: http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/web-scripts/taxes/version-13/public/
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1

> curl -I http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/web-scripts/taxes/version-13/public/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8
  • Line 4: the redirection of the first rule in the [.htaccess] file;
  • line 11: the redirection from the script [public/index.php].

In a browser, the URL that launches the HTML application becomes [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/]. After the two redirects, the authentication page appears, along with its logo:

The application works the same as the one in version 12. Here is the tax calculation screen after a simulation:

The URL client requests for JSON and XML have changed: the primary controller is now [.../version-13/public/main.php]. To use the JSON client from version 12 with the version 13 server, simply change the [urlServer] key in its configuration file.

docs.title: 24.5. In production: the document root is the [public] folder
docs.text:
The [.htaccess] file is a solution adapted from [Laragon], where a single folder, [www], contains multiple applications. On a production server, the approach is different: the [public] folder is made the document root for the site. The rest of the application is then outside the website’s directory structure: no URL can access it, and no rules are necessary. This is the organization recommended by the PHP frameworks.

With [Apache], you define a virtual host, c.-à-d, for this purpose—an additional website served by the same server, [Apache]. The file [Config/vhost-impots-v13.conf] provides an example:

# an Apache virtual host whose document root is the [public] folder in version 13
# to be placed in the [<laragon>/etc/apache2/sites-enabled] folder (paths to be adjusted)
# The application is then accessible at URL [http://localhost:8013/]
Listen 8013
<VirtualHost *:8013>
     # the document root: only the contents of [public] are accessible via the web
    DocumentRoot "C:/laragon/www/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public"
    <Directory "C:/laragon/www/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-13/public">
         # No [.htaccess] file to read: the configuration is here
        AllowOverride None
        Options -Indexes
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
  • Line 4: [Apache] also listens on port 8013. A virtual host can be distinguished from others by its port, as shown here, or by its name ([impots.test], for example). Using the port avoids having to declare a new hostname;
  • Lines 5–14: The configuration of the virtual host that responds to requests received on port 8013;
  • line 7: The document root for this site is the [public] folder in version 13. URL and [http://localhost:8013/main.php] therefore refer to the file [public/main.php];
  • Lines 8–13: Access rights to the [public] folder. [AllowOverride None] tells [Apache] that it does not need to search for [.htaccess] files: the entire configuration is here, which is also faster.

In [Laragon], place such a file—adjusting the paths to the installation folder of [Laragon]—in the [<laragon>/etc/apache2/sites-enabled] folder, then restart [Apache] from the [Laragon] window (click the [Stop] button, then the [Start All] button). You will then have:

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Location: main.php?action=init-session&type=html
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

> curl "http://localhost:8013/main.php?action=init-session&type=json"
{"action":"init-session","état":700,"réponse":"session démarrée avec type [json]"}

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/Resources/logo.jpg
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Last-Modified: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 16:39:23 GMT
ETag: "1410-65cca0eef010c"
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Length: 5136
Content-Type: image/jpeg

> curl -I http://localhost:8013/Config/config.json
HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
Server: Apache/2.4.58
Content-Type: text/html; charset=iso-8859-1
  • lines 1–6: the site’s URL is served by the [public/index.php] script;
  • lines 8–9: the main controller responds normally;
  • lines 11–18: the logo is served;
  • lines 20–23: the configuration file is no longer rejected; it simply does not exist for the web server: the response is [404 Not Found]. The file [.htaccess] in the [version-13] folder is not read, since it is outside the document root.

In both cases—whether it’s [Laragon] with the file [.htaccess] or a virtual host whose root is the folder [public]—the application code is the same. That is the benefit of the new directory structure: public content is gathered in a single folder, and everything else is protected by default.

docs.title: 8. Practical Exercise – Version 3
docs.text:
We’ll revisit the exercise we covered earlier (versions 1 and 2) and solve it using code PHP that employs classes. We’ll put into practice what we’ve learned in the previous three chapters:

  • an (immutable) [readonly] class to represent tax administration data;
  • an interface, an abstract class that partially implements it, and a derived class that completes it;
  • a single exception type, [ExceptionImpots], to report all application errors;
  • the [#[\Override]] attribute on all methods that implement an interface method or override a parent method.

docs.title: 8.1. The script directory structure
docs.text:
Version 3 is located in the [scripts-console/impots/version-03] folder:

version-03
├── AbstractBaseImpots.php
├── errors.txt
├── ExceptionImpots.php
├── ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile.php
├── InterfaceImpots.php
├── main.php
├── resultats.txt
├── taxadmindata.json
├── TaxAdminData.php
├── taxpayersdata.txt
├── test-taxadmindata.php
└── Utilitaires.php

Each class or interface is in a file that bears its name. This is a convention universally followed in PHP (it is even mandated by the automatic loading standard PSR-4, which we will encounter with [Composer]).

docs.title: 8.2. The [ExceptionImpots] Exception
docs.text:
In version 3, when a class constructor or method encounters an error, it will throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// The exception thrown by the classes in the tax calculation application
class ExceptionImpots extends \RuntimeException
{
     // No code: the constructor inherited from [\RuntimeException] is sufficient
     // __construct(string $message = "", int $code = 0, ?\Throwable $previous = null)
}

Comments

  • Line 6: The class [ExceptionImpots] is in the [Application] namespace. All classes and interfaces in the tax calculation application will be in this namespace;
  • line 9: The class [ExceptionImpots] extends the predefined class PHP [RuntimeException]. As we saw in the chapter on exceptions, an exception is primarily defined by its type: it is the type that allows it to be caught with a [catch (ExceptionImpots $ex)] clause;
  • Lines 11–12: The PHP 7 course defined a constructor [__construct(string $message, int $code = 0)] that simply called the parent class’s constructor. It is unnecessary: the class inherits the constructor from [RuntimeException], which accepts a message, an error code, and any previous exception. We’ll use this last parameter to encapsulate a low-level exception (a [JsonException], for example) within a [ExceptionImpots].

docs.title: 8.3. The [TaxAdminData] class
docs.text:
In version 2, the tax administration data was consolidated:

  • first in a JSON file;
  • then from this JSON file into an associative array.

We had noted a flaw in this solution: there is no guarantee that the associative array contains all the expected keys or that the associated values are numbers. In version 3, the tax authority data is still in the file [taxadmindata.json] but with different attribute names, written according to the camelCase convention for class attribute names:

{
    "limites": [9964, 27519, 73779, 156244, 0],
    "coeffR": [0, 0.14, 0.3, 0.41, 0.45],
    "coeffN": [0, 1394.96, 5798, 13913.69, 20163.45],
    "plafondQfDemiPart": 1551,
    "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": 21037,
    "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42074,
    "valeurReducDemiPart": 3797,
    "plafondDecoteCelibataire": 1196,
    "plafondDecoteCouple": 1970,
    "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote": 2627,
    "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": 1595,
    "abattementDixPourcentMax": 12502,
    "abattementDixPourcentMin": 437
}

In version 2, this file was used to initialize an associative array. In version 3, it will initialize an object of the following class: [TaxAdminData]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// tax administration data: an immutable object
final readonly class TaxAdminData
{
     // the names of arrays and constants expected in the data
    private const array TABLEAUX = ["limites", "coeffR", "coeffN"];
    private const array CONSTANTES = [
        "plafondQfDemiPart",
        "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
        "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
        "valeurReducDemiPart",
        "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
        "plafondDecoteCouple",
        "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
        "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
        "abattementDixPourcentMax",
        "abattementDixPourcentMin",
    ];

     // private constructor: you must use the methods [from...]
    private function __construct(
         // tax brackets
        public array $limites,
        public array $coeffR,
        public array $coeffN,
         // tax calculation constants
        public float $plafondQfDemiPart,
        public float $plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction,
        public float $plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction,
        public float $valeurReducDemiPart,
        public float $plafondDecoteCelibataire,
        public float $plafondDecoteCouple,
        public float $plafondImpotCouplePourDecote,
        public float $plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote,
        public float $abattementDixPourcentMax,
        public float $abattementDixPourcentMin,
    ) {
    }

     // Generation from a file JSON
    public static function fromJsonFile(string $taxAdminDataFilename): self
    {
         // retrieve the contents of the tax data file
        $fileContents = is_readable($taxAdminDataFilename) ? file_get_contents($taxAdminDataFilename) : false;
         // error?
        if ($fileContents === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier des données [$taxAdminDataFilename] n'existe pas", 1);
        }
         // Decode the JSON into an associative array
        try {
            $data = json_decode($fileContents, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier de données JSON [$taxAdminDataFilename] n'a pu être exploité correctement", 2, $ex);
        }
         // JSON must be an object {...}
        if (!is_array($data)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier de données JSON [$taxAdminDataFilename] ne contient pas un objet JSON", 3);
        }
         // constructing the object from the associative array
        return self::fromArray($data);
    }

     // constructing from an associative array [nom => valeur]
    public static function fromArray(array $data): self
    {
         // The keys present must be exactly those expected
        $attendues = [...self::TABLEAUX, ...self::CONSTANTES];
        $manquante = array_first(array_diff($attendues, array_keys($data)));
        if ($manquante !== null) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("L'attribut [$manquante] de [TaxAdminData] n'a pas été initialisé", 4);
        }
        $inconnue = array_first(array_diff(array_keys($data), $attendues));
        if ($inconnue !== null) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("L'attribut [$inconnue] n'existe pas dans [TaxAdminData]", 5);
        }
         // Each value is checked and converted
        $valeurs = [];
        foreach (self::TABLEAUX as $clé) {
             // a non-empty array of real numbers >= 0
            if (!is_array($data[$clé]) || !array_is_list($data[$clé]) || count($data[$clé]) === 0) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("La valeur de l'attribut [$clé] est invalide", 6);
            }
            $valeurs[$clé] = array_map(fn(mixed $valeur): float => self::check($clé, $valeur), $data[$clé]);
        }
         // The three arrays must be the same size
        $taille = count($valeurs["limites"]);
        if (count($valeurs["coeffR"]) !== $taille || count($valeurs["coeffN"]) !== $taille) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Les tableaux [limites, coeffR, coeffN] n'ont pas la même taille", 7);
        }
        foreach (self::CONSTANTES as $clé) {
             // a real number >= 0
            $valeurs[$clé] = self::check($clé, $data[$clé]);
        }
         // object construction: the array keys become named arguments
        return new self(...$valeurs);
    }

     // checks whether a value is a positive real number or zero and returns it in the form of [float]
    private static function check(string $clé, mixed $value): float
    {
         // accepts 1551, 1551.78, "1551" but not "xx", true, null, -3...
        if ((is_int($value) || is_float($value) || (is_string($value) && is_numeric($value)))
            && (float) $value >= 0) {
            return (float) $value;
        }
        throw new ExceptionImpots("La valeur de l'attribut [$clé] est invalide", 6);
    }

     // string JSON of the object
    public function __toString(): string
    {
        return json_encode(get_object_vars($this), JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    }
}

Comments

  • Line 9: The class is [readonly]: All of its attributes are read-only. Once created, a [TaxAdminData] object can no longer be modified: it can be safely shared among all parts of the application. It is also [final]: it cannot be derived;
  • lines 12–24: two private class constants list the names of the attributes expected in the data. Starting with PHP 8.3, a class constant can be typed (here, [array]);
  • lines 27–43: The constructor uses parameter promotion: each parameter becomes a public attribute with the same name and type. The attributes have the same names as the keys in the JSON file. This is an important point that greatly simplifies code writing, as we will see. The tax brackets are arrays ([array]), and the calculation constants are real numbers ([float]). In PHP 7, attributes could not be typed (as noted in the PHP 7 course); they can be typed starting with PHP 7.4;
  • Line 27: The constructor is private; [new TaxAdminData(...)] cannot be written outside the class. A [TaxAdminData] object can only be obtained through the static methods [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray], which verify the validity of the data. This ensures that every [TaxAdminData] object contains valid data. In PHP, a class can have only one constructor. Static methods that construct an object—sometimes called “named constructors”—allow for multiple ways to construct an object. Course PHP 7 used instance methods [setFromJsonFile] called on an empty object: [(new TaxAdminData())->setFromJsonFile(...)]. This is impossible with an immutable object;
  • Lines 47–67: The [fromJsonFile] method constructs a [TaxAdminData] object from the JSON file, whose name is passed to it. Its return type, [self], refers to the class itself;
  • lines 50–53: The file’s contents are read. If this is not possible, a [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown. This exception will propagate up to the main script;
  • lines 56–60: The file’s content, JSON, is decoded. With the option [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] (PHP 7.3), the [json_decode] function throws a [JsonException] exception when the JSON is invalid, instead of silently returning [null]. Note the named argument [flags:], which avoids having to assign a value to the third parameter [depth] of [json_decode]. The exception [JsonException] is encapsulated within a [ExceptionImpots]: the calling code only has to handle one exception type but can determine the original cause using [$ex->getPrevious()];
  • lines 62–64: a file containing, for example, only the number 12 is a valid JSON; you must verify that an array has indeed been obtained;
  • line 66: the rest of the work is delegated to the [fromArray] method. This method is public: it may be used in a future version where tax administration data comes from a database;
  • Lines 73–81: We verify that the keys in the array [$data] are exactly the expected names. [[...self::TABLEAUX, ...self::CONSTANTES]] creates an array containing the elements from both arrays. The function [array_diff] removes the elements from the first table that are not present in the second, and the function [array_first] (PHP 8.5) returns the first element of an array or [null] if the array is empty. This detects a missing key followed by an unknown key. This is the most common error: a typo in an attribute name in the [taxadmindata.json] file. In course PHP 7, the loop [$this->$key = $value] silently created a dynamic attribute with the incorrect name. Since PHP 8.2, the creation of dynamic attributes has been deprecated, and it is prohibited within a [readonly] class;
  • lines 84–90: Each of the three arrays must be a non-empty list (function [array_is_list], PHP 8.1) whose elements are all positive or zero real numbers. The function [array_map] applies the method [check] to each element;
  • lines 92–95: The three tax bracket arrays must be the same size;
  • lines 96–99: Each of the calculation constants must be a positive real number or zero;
  • Line 101: The array [$valeurs] uses the names of the constructor’s parameters as keys. The operator [...], when applied to an array with string keys, converts each element into a named argument (PHP 8.1): this line is equivalent to [new self(limites: $valeurs["limites"], coeffR: $valeurs["coeffR"], ...)]. This is where choosing identical names for the JSON keys and the class attributes simplifies the code;
  • Lines 105–113: The method [check] checks whether a value [$value] of unknown type ([mixed]) is a positive number or zero. According to the information in the JSON file, the value read can be an integer (1551), a floating-point number (1551.78), a string convertible to a number ("1551"), a non-convertible string ("xx"), a Boolean... The function [is_numeric] returns [true] for a string representing a number. The PHP 7 course performed this check using a regular expression and returned a [stdClass] object indicating whether an error had occurred. Here, an error triggers an exception, and the method simply returns the number in the form of a [float];
  • Line 116: The [__toString] method returns the JSON string containing the object’s attributes. The [get_object_vars] function returns a [nom de l'attribut => valeur] associative array.

docs.title: 8.3.1. Why are there no longer any getters and setters?
docs.text:
Course PHP 7 declared the attributes as private and wrote a getter and a setter for each one (26 methods), automatically generated by IDE and NetBeans. The setters were “fluent”: they returned the [$this] object, which allowed for chained calls to [$data->setLimites($limites)->setCoeffR($coeffR)].

With PHP 8, this code is no longer necessary:

  • the getters were used to read private attributes. The attributes [readonly] can safely be made public since they cannot be modified: we write [$taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart] instead of [$taxAdminData->getPlafondQfDemiPart()];
  • the setters were used to initialize the object and allowed for value validation. An immutable object is initialized once and for all by its constructor, and validation is performed by the methods [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray];
  • Typed attributes guarantee the type of the values. The PHP 7 course noted that the [$this->plafondQfDemiPart = 'abcd'] statement was possible: with attributes [float] and [declare(strict_types=1)], it causes an error [TypeError].

The script [test-taxadmindata.php] verifies the functionality of the class [TaxAdminData]:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of function parameters and return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// class inclusion
require_once __DIR__ . "/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/TaxAdminData.php";

// a valid object
$taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("taxadmindata.json");
print "$taxAdminData\n";
print "plafondQfDemiPart=" . $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart . "\n";
// The object is immutable
try {
    $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart = 2000;
} catch (\Error $ex) {
    print $ex::class . " : " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
}
// the constructor is private
try {
    $taxAdminData = new TaxAdminData([], [], []);
} catch (\Error $ex) {
    print $ex::class . " : " . $ex->getMessage() . "\n";
}

// invalid data
$valides = json_decode(file_get_contents("taxadmindata.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
$tests = [
     // file does not exist
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("xx.json"),
     // file that is not of type JSON
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile("taxpayersdata.txt"),
     // missing key
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(array_diff_key($valides, ["plafondQfDemiPart" => 0])),
     // unknown key (typo)
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQFDemiPart" => 1551] + $valides),
     // non-numeric value
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQfDemiPart" => "xx"] + $valides),
     // negative value in an array
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["coeffR" => [0, 0.14, -0.3, 0.41, 0.45]] + $valides),
     // arrays of different sizes
    fn() => TaxAdminData::fromArray(["limites" => [9964, 27519, 73779, 0]] + $valides),
];
foreach ($tests as $test) {
    try {
        $test();
    } catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
        print "ExceptionImpots n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
    }
}
// the value "1551" is accepted and converted to a real number
$taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray(["plafondQfDemiPart" => "1551"] + $valides);
var_dump($taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);

Comments

  • line 14: construction of a valid [TaxAdminData] object from the [taxadmindata.json] file;
  • line 15: the object is inserted into a string: its [__toString] method is called;
  • line 19: attempt to modify a read-only attribute;
  • line 25: attempt to use the private constructor;
  • line 31: the associative array of valid data;
  • lines 32–47: an array of arrow functions, each constructing a [TaxAdminData] object from invalid data. The invalid data is obtained by modifying a copy of the [$valides] array. When applying the [+] operator to two arrays, the elements of the left array take precedence in the event of a common key. The function [array_diff_key] makes the first array private to the keys present in the second;
  • lines 48–54: Each function is executed, and the expected exception is displayed;
  • line 56: a numeric string is accepted and converted to a real number.

Results:

> php test-taxadmindata.php
{"limites":[9964,27519,73779,156244,0],"coeffR":[0,0.14,0.3,0.41,0.45],"coeffN":[0,1394.96,5798,13913.69,20163.45],"plafondQfDemiPart":1551,"plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction":21037,"plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction":42074,"valeurReducDemiPart":3797,"plafondDecoteCelibataire":1196,"plafondDecoteCouple":1970,"plafondImpotCouplePourDecote":2627,"plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote":1595,"abattementDixPourcentMax":12502,"abattementDixPourcentMin":437}
plafondQfDemiPart=1551
Error : Cannot modify readonly property Application\TaxAdminData::$plafondQfDemiPart
Error : Call to private Application\TaxAdminData::__construct() from global scope
ExceptionImpots n° 1 : Le fichier des données [xx.json] n'existe pas
ExceptionImpots n° 2 : Le fichier de données JSON [taxpayersdata.txt] n'a pu être exploité correctement
ExceptionImpots n° 4 : L'attribut [plafondQfDemiPart] de [TaxAdminData] n'a pas été initialisé
ExceptionImpots n° 5 : L'attribut [plafondQFDemiPart] n'existe pas dans [TaxAdminData]
ExceptionImpots n° 6 : La valeur de l'attribut [plafondQfDemiPart] est invalide
ExceptionImpots n° 6 : La valeur de l'attribut [coeffR] est invalide
ExceptionImpots n° 7 : Les tableaux [limites, coeffR, coeffN] n'ont pas la même taille
float(1551)
  • line 2: the object’s JSON string. Note that real numbers without a decimal part (1551.0) are written without it (1551) by the [json_encode] function;
  • Lines 4–5: The two [Error] errors caused by modifying a [readonly] attribute and by calling a private constructor. These are programming errors, not data errors: they are not converted to [ExceptionImpots];
  • Lines 6–12: All incorrect data is detected, each with a different message and error code;
  • line 13: the string "1551" has been converted to a floating-point number.

docs.title: 8.4. The [InterfaceImpots] interface
docs.text:
We will now define the following [InterfaceImpots] interface: [InterfaceImpots.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

interface InterfaceImpots
{
     // retrieve data from the tax authority to calculate the tax
     // may trigger the exception ExceptionImpots
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

     // the interface can calculate tax
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

     // The interface can process data from text files
     // $taxPayersFileName: taxpayer data file containing marital status, number of children, and annual salary
     // $resultsFileName: results file containing marital status, number of children, annual salary, tax amount, etc.
     // $errorsFileName: file containing errors encountered
     // may trigger the exception ExceptionImpots
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void;
}

Comments

  • line 8: the interface for calculating taxes. It is also in the [Application] namespace;
  • line 12: The method [getTaxAdminData] will retrieve data from the tax authority into an object of type [TaxAdminData], which we just introduced. Since this data may be stored in a file, a database, or even on the network, the method [getTaxAdminData] may fail to retrieve the data. In this case, it will throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots]. This is the standard method in object-oriented programming for signaling an error encountered in a method or a constructor;
  • line 15: The [calculerImpot] method will calculate a taxpayer’s tax;
  • line 22: The method [executeBatchImpots] calculates the tax for multiple taxpayers;
    • [$taxPayersFileName] is the name of the text file containing the taxpayers’ data;
    • [$resultsFileName] is the name of the text file containing the tax amounts for these taxpayers;
    • [$errorsFileName] is the name of the text file containing the errors encountered while processing these files.

The contents of the taxpayer text file [taxpayersdata.txt] are as follows:

oui,2,55555
oui,2,50000
oui,3,50000
non,2,100000
non,3x,100000
non,3,100000
oui,3,100000
oui,5,100000x
oui,5,100000
non,0,100000
oui,2,30000
non,0,200000
oui,3,200000

Note that lines 5 and 8 contain incorrect entries. The other eleven lines correspond to the eleven taxpayers listed in the table of official figures.

docs.title: 8.5. The class [Utilitaires]
docs.text:
We also define a class named [Utilitaires] in a file named [Utilitaires.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// a utility class: it is neither instantiable nor derivable
final class Utilitaires
{
     // private constructor: the class cannot be instantiated
    private function __construct()
    {
    }

    public static function cutNewLineChar(string $ligne): string
    {
         // the end-of-line character in $ligne is removed if it exists
         // (\r\n on Windows, \n on Unix)
        return rtrim($ligne, "\r\n");
    }
}

Comments

  • Line 9: The class [Utilitaires] is also placed in the [Application] namespace. It contains only static methods: there is no reason to instantiate or derive from it. The course PHP 7 declared it abstract to prevent its instantiation, regretting that PHP refused to declare it as both [final] and [abstract]. This is still the case. The current practice is to declare it as [final] (non-derivable) and give it a private constructor (which cannot be instantiated from outside);
  • line 16: the method [cutNewLineChar] removes any line-end characters from the text passed to it as a parameter. It is a static method, meaning it will be called in the form [Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar($ligne)]. Its code is the same as that of the function of the same name in version 2.

docs.title: 8.6. The abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots]
docs.text:
The [InterfaceImpots] interface will be implemented by the following abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots] [AbstractBaseImpots.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// an abstract class that implements the [InterfaceImpots] interface
abstract class AbstractBaseImpots implements InterfaceImpots
{
     // tax administration data
    private ?TaxAdminData $taxAdminData = null;

     // data required to calculate the tax: derived classes know where to find it
     #[\Override]
    abstract public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

     // Tax calculation
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
         // $marié: yes, no
         // $enfants: number of children
         // $salaire: annual salary
         // $this->taxAdminData: data from the tax authorities
        //
         // Retrieve tax authority data if it hasn't already been done
        $this->taxAdminData ??= $this->getTaxAdminData();
         // Calculate tax with children
        $result1 = $this->calculerImpot2($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
        $impot1 = $result1["impôt"];
         // Calculate tax without children
        if ($enfants !== 0) {
            $result2 = $this->calculerImpot2($marié, 0, $salaire);
            $impot2 = $result2["impôt"];
             // Apply the family quotient cap
            $plafondDemiPart = $this->taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart;
            if ($enfants < 3) {
                 // plafondQfDemiPart euros for the first 2 children
                $impot2 = $impot2 - $enfants * $plafondDemiPart;
            } else {
                 // plafondQfDemiPart euros for the first two children, double that amount for subsequent children
                $impot2 = $impot2 - 2 * $plafondDemiPart - ($enfants - 2) * 2 * $plafondDemiPart;
            }
        } else {
            $impot2 = $impot1;
            $result2 = $result1;
        }
         // We use the highest tax amount with the corresponding rate and surcharge
        if ($impot1 > $impot2) {
            $impot = $impot1;
            $taux = $result1["taux"];
            $surcôte = $result1["surcôte"];
        } else {
            $surcôte = $impot2 - $impot1 + $result2["surcôte"];
            $impot = $impot2;
            $taux = $result2["taux"];
        }
         // Calculation of a possible tax reduction
        $décôte = $this->getDecote($marié, $salaire, $impot);
        $impot -= $décôte;
         // Calculation of a potential tax reduction
        $réduction = $this->getRéduction($marié, $salaire, $enfants, $impot);
        $impot -= $réduction;
         // Result
        return [
            "impôt" => (int) floor($impot),
            "surcôte" => (int) $surcôte,
            "décôte" => (int) $décôte,
            "réduction" => (int) $réduction,
            "taux" => $taux,
        ];
    }

Comments

  • line 9: The class [AbstractBaseImpots] implements the interface [InterfaceImpots];
  • Line 12: Data from the tax authority will be stored in the private attribute [$taxAdminData]. Its type, [?TaxAdminData], means “a [TaxAdminData] object or the value [null].” Its initial value is [null];
  • line 16: the [getTaxAdminData] method of the interface. We do not yet know how to define it: we have seen a case where data from the tax authority was retrieved from a JSON file (version 2). We will see another case where the data will be retrieved from a database. It will be up to the derived classes to define the content of the [getTaxAdminData] method. The method is therefore declared abstract, which requires the class itself to be declared abstract. This declaration is optional: an abstract class that implements an interface is not required to redeclare the methods it does not implement. However, it makes the code more readable. The attribute [#[\Override]] (PHP 8.3) indicates that the method belongs to an interface or a parent class: if the name is incorrect, PHP signals the error;
  • Lines 21–73: The tax calculation function already encountered in versions 1 and 2. Its parameters have changed: Version 2 took the associative array [$taxAdminData] as its first parameter, while Version 3 uses the attribute [$this->taxAdminData]. The first difference between these two solutions is a difference in the visibility of tax data:
    • in version 2, the associative array [$taxAdminData] did not have global visibility. It was therefore passed as a parameter to all tax calculation functions;
    • in version 3, the attribute [$this->taxAdminData] is visible in all methods of the class. It is therefore no longer passed as a parameter;
  • A second difference stems from the fact that version 3 replaces functions with class methods. Each method call is now made using the expression [$this->méthode(...)] (line 31, line 61);
  • Line 29: A third difference is that when the [calculerImpot] method begins its work, it does not know whether the [$taxAdminData] attribute it needs has been initialized. In fact, the class has no constructor that would initialize it. It is therefore up to the [calculerImpot] method to do so using the [getTaxAdminData] method. The operator [??=] (PHP 7.4) assigns the value on the right to the variable on the left only if the variable is equal to [null]. The line is equivalent to [if ($this->taxAdminData === null) { $this->taxAdminData = $this->getTaxAdminData(); }];
  • Line 38: Data from the tax authority is read directly from the read-only public attributes of the object [TaxAdminData];
  • Apart from these differences, the tax calculation method remains the same as in previous versions.

The private methods for calculating tax are as follows:

    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    private function calculerImpot2(string $marié, int $enfants, float $salaire): array
    {
         // number of shares
        $nbParts = match ($marié) {
            "oui" => $enfants / 2 + 2,
            "non" => $enfants / 2 + 1,
        };
         // 1 share per child starting with the third
        if ($enfants >= 3) {
             // half an additional share for each child starting with the third
            $nbParts += 0.5 * ($enfants - 2);
        }
         // taxable income
        $revenuImposable = $this->getRevenuImposable($salaire);
         // surcharge
        $surcôte = floor($revenuImposable - 0.9 * $salaire);
         // for rounding issues
        if ($surcôte < 0) {
            $surcôte = 0;
        }
         // family quotient
        $quotient = $revenuImposable / $nbParts;
         // tax brackets (copies of the object's tables)
        $limites = $this->taxAdminData->limites;
        $coeffR = $this->taxAdminData->coeffR;
        $coeffN = $this->taxAdminData->coeffN;
         // is placed at the end of the limits table to stop the following loop
        $limites[count($limites) - 1] = $quotient;
         // tax calculation
        $i = 0;
        while ($quotient > $limites[$i]) {
            $i++;
        }
         // Now we can calculate the tax
        $impôt = floor($revenuImposable * $coeffR[$i] - $nbParts * $coeffN[$i]);
         // result
        return ["impôt" => $impôt, "surcôte" => $surcôte, "taux" => $coeffR[$i]];
    }

     // revenuImposable = annual salary - deduction
     // The deduction has a minimum and a maximum
    private function getRevenuImposable(float $salaire): float
    {
         // a deduction of 10% of the salary, limited by a minimum and a maximum
        $abattement = 0.1 * $salaire;
        $abattement = min($abattement, $this->taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMax);
        $abattement = max($abattement, $this->taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMin);
         // taxable income
        $revenuImposable = $salaire - $abattement;
         // Result
        return floor($revenuImposable);
    }

     // Calculates a possible discount
    private function getDecote(string $marié, float $salaire, float $impots): float
    {
         // Initially, a zero discount
        $décôte = 0;
         // maximum tax amount to qualify for the tax reduction
        $plafondImpôtPourDécôte = $marié === "oui"
            ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondImpotCouplePourDecote
            : $this->taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote;
        if ($impots < $plafondImpôtPourDécôte) {
             // maximum discount amount
            $plafondDécôte = $marié === "oui"
                ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple
                : $this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire;
             // theoretical discount
            $décôte = $plafondDécôte - 0.75 * $impots;
             // The discount cannot exceed the tax amount
            if ($décôte > $impots) {
                $décôte = $impots;
            }
             // No discount < 0
            if ($décôte < 0) {
                $décôte = 0;
            }
        }
         // Result
        return ceil($décôte);
    }

     // calculates a possible reduction
    private function getRéduction(string $marié, float $salaire, int $enfants, float $impots): float
    {
         // the income threshold for eligibility for the 20% reduction
        $plafondRevenuPourRéduction = $marié === "oui"
            ? $this->taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction
            : $this->taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction;
        $plafondRevenuPourRéduction += $enfants * $this->taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart;
        if ($enfants > 2) {
            $plafondRevenuPourRéduction += ($enfants - 2) * $this->taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart;
        }
         // taxable income
        $revenuImposable = $this->getRevenuImposable($salaire);
         // reduction
        $réduction = 0;
        if ($revenuImposable < $plafondRevenuPourRéduction) {
             // 20% reduction
            $réduction = 0.2 * $impots;
        }
         // result
        return ceil($réduction);
    }

Comments

  • Lines 80–83: The expression [match] (PHP 8.0) is a better replacement for [if / else] from version 2. It compares the value [$marié] to the values of its branches using the equality operator [===] and returns the value of the matching branch. If no branch matches, it raises an error [UnhandledMatchError]: a marital status other than “yes” or “no” will not go unnoticed;
  • lines 100–102: the tax bracket tables are copied into local variables. In PHP, assigning a table creates a copy: the modification to [$limites] on line 104 does not affect the [readonly] attribute of the [TaxAdminData] object (which would, incidentally, be an error);
  • Lines 122–123: The functions [min] and [max] replace the two [if] functions from version 2: the deduction cannot exceed [abattementDixPourcentMax] or be less than [abattementDixPourcentMin];
  • the rest of the code is the same as in version 2, where the expression [$taxAdminData["PLAFOND_DECOTE_COUPLE"]] has become [$this->taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple]. A typo in an attribute name is now flagged by the [VS Code] editor ([PHP Intelephense] extension) as soon as the code is written, which was not the case for a typo in an array key.

The [executeBatchImpots] method is as follows:

     // Batch tax calculation
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
         // The three files are not yet open
        $errors = $results = $data = false;
         // Quite a few errors can occur when managing files
        try {
             // Opening the error file
            $errors = fopen($errorsFileName, "w");
            if ($errors === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible de créer le fichier des erreurs [$errorsFileName]", 10);
            }
             // opening the results file
            $results = fopen($resultsFileName, "w");
            if ($results === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible de créer le fichier des résultats [$resultsFileName]", 11);
            }
             // Opening the taxpayer data file
            $data = is_readable($taxPayersFileName) ? fopen($taxPayersFileName, "r") : false;
            if ($data === false) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Impossible d'ouvrir en lecture les déclarations des contribuables [$taxPayersFileName]", 12);
            }
             // Processing the current row of the taxpayer data file
             // which has the format: marital status, number of children, annual salary
            $num = 0;         // current line number
            $nbErreurs = 0;   // Number of errors encountered
            while (($ligne = fgets($data, 100)) !== false) {
                 // one more row
                $num++;
                 // Remove any end-of-row marker
                $ligne = Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar($ligne);
                 // empty lines are ignored
                if (trim($ligne) === "") {
                    continue;
                }
                 // The line must contain the three fields: married, children, salary
                $champs = array_map(trim(...), explode(",", $ligne));
                $erreur = count($champs) !== 3;
                if (!$erreur) {
                    [$marié, $enfants, $salaire] = $champs;
                     // the marital status must be "yes" or "no"
                    $marié = strtolower($marié);
                     // The number of children and the salary must be positive integers or zero
                    $erreur = !in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)
                        || !preg_match('/^\d+$/', $enfants)
                        || !preg_match('/^\d+$/', $salaire);
                }
                 // Error?
                if ($erreur) {
                    fputs($errors, "la ligne [$num] du fichier [$taxPayersFileName] est erronée\n");
                    $nbErreurs++;
                    continue;
                }
                 // Calculate the tax
                $result = $this->calculerImpot($marié, (int) $enfants, (int) $salaire);
                 // The result is written to the results file
                $result = ["marié" => $marié, "enfants" => (int) $enfants, "salaire" => (int) $salaire] + $result;
                fputs($results, json_encode($result, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR) . "\n");
            }
             // Any errors?
            if ($nbErreurs > 0) {
                throw new ExceptionImpots("Il y a eu $nbErreurs ligne(s) erronée(s) : voir le fichier [$errorsFileName]", 15);
            }
        } finally {
             // Closing the files that were opened
            foreach ([$data, $results, $errors] as $fichier) {
                if ($fichier !== false) {
                    fclose($fichier);
                }
            }
        }
    }

Code comments

  • Line 185: The method takes three parameters:
    • [$taxPayersFileName]: the name of the text file containing taxpayer data. Each line of text contains data for one taxpayer in the following format: marital status (yes/no), number of children, annual salary; for example, [oui,2,55555];
    • [$resultsFileName]: the name of the text file that will contain the results. Each line of text will be the string JSON representing a taxpayer’s results, for example, [{"marié":"oui","enfants":2,"salaire":50000,"impôt":1384,"surcôte":0,"décôte":384,"réduction":347,"taux":0.14}];
    • [$errorsFileName]: the name of the text file containing errors, for example, [la ligne [5] du fichier [taxpayersdata.txt] est erronée];
  • line 188: the variables for the three files are initialized to [false] (file not open). This will make it possible to determine, in the [finally] clause, which files have been opened;
  • line 190: Because a number of operations can throw an exception, a [try / finally] structure encloses the entire method code;
  • lines 192–204: The three files are opened. An exception is thrown as soon as an open operation fails, with a different error code for each case;
  • Line 210: The lines in the [$data] file are read one by one in blocks of up to 100 characters (all lines are less than 100 characters long);
  • Line 214: The static method [Utilitaires::cutNewLineChar] is used to remove any end-of-line characters;
  • Lines 216–218: Empty lines (for example, at the end of the file) are ignored;
  • line 220: the line is split at the comma, and the spaces surrounding each field are removed. [trim(...)] is the syntax for “first-class callables” (PHP 8.1): it refers to the [trim] function itself, without calling it;
  • line 221: the line must have exactly three fields. The PHP 7 course wrote [list($marié, $enfants, $salaire) = explode(",", $ligne)] directly: with a line having only two fields, PHP 8 issues a “Undefined array key 2” warning;
  • Lines 227–229: The validity of the three elements is checked: marital status must be “yes” or “no,” and the number of children and salary must be positive integers or zero (a sequence of digits, regular expression [/^\d+$/]). The third parameter [true] of [in_array] requires a strict comparison [===];
  • lines 232–236: no exception is thrown if the line is invalid; instead, an error message is written to the text file [$errors], and the program moves on to the next line;
  • line 238: if the line read is valid, the tax is calculated. The result is returned as an associative array [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux];
  • line 240: The keys [marié, enfants, salaire] are added to the beginning of the result;
  • line 241: the result is written to the text file [$results] in the form of its string JSON. The option [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] causes the function [json_encode] to throw an exception [JsonException] rather than returning [false] if the encoding fails;
  • lines 244–246: At the end of processing the [$data] file, the number of erroneous lines encountered is checked. If there is at least one, an exception is thrown;
  • lines 247–254: Regardless of how the method’s execution ends (normally or via an exception), the clause [finally] is executed: any files that were opened are closed. Course PHP 7 used a structure [try / catch / finally] whose clause [catch] simply rethrew the exception. This is unnecessary: a [try / finally] structure without [catch] allows the exception to propagate after the [finally] clause has been executed. Furthermore, the PHP 7 course closed the three files without verifying that they had been opened: in PHP 8, [fclose(false)] causes a [TypeError] error.

docs.title: 8.7. The [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class
docs.text:
The abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots] does not implement the [getTaxAdminData] method of the [InterfaceImpots] interface. We must therefore define it in a derived class. We do this in the following derived class, [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// A class that retrieves data from the tax authority in a file JSON
class ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile extends AbstractBaseImpots
{
     // data from the tax authority
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

     // the constructor
    public function __construct(string $jsonFileName)
    {
         // $this->taxAdminData is initialized from the file JSON
         // may throw a ExceptionImpots exception
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile($jsonFileName);
    }

     // returns the data used to calculate the tax
     #[\Override]
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData
    {
        return $this->taxAdminData;
    }
}

Comments

  • Line 9: The [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class extends the abstract class [AbstractBaseImpots]. It must define the [getTaxAdminData] method, which its parent class has not defined;
  • Line 12: The attribute [$taxAdminData] will contain data from the tax authority. It is read-only: it is initialized once and for all by the constructor. Note that the parent class also has a private attribute [$taxAdminData]: the two attributes are distinct, as a private attribute is visible only within the class that declares it;
  • lines 15–20: The constructor receives as its only parameter the name of the file JSON containing the tax data;
  • line 19: An object of type [TaxAdminData] is created from the file JSON. This operation may throw an exception of type [ExceptionImpots]. This exception will propagate up to the main script [main.php];
  • Lines 23–27: A body is provided for the [getTaxAdminData] method, which the parent class had not defined. Here, it is sufficient to ensure that the [$this->taxAdminData] attribute is initialized by the constructor.

docs.title: 8.8. The script [main.php]
docs.text:
These classes and interfaces are used by the following script, [main.php]:

<?php

// strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// inclusion of interfaces and classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/InterfaceImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/AbstractBaseImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile.php";

// Definition of constants
const TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME = "taxpayersdata.txt";
const RESULTS_FILENAME = "resultats.txt";
const ERRORS_FILENAME = "errors.txt";
const TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME = "taxadmindata.json";

try {
     // an object is created [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile]
    $impots = new ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile(TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME);
     // running the tax batch
    $impots->executeBatchImpots(TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME, RESULTS_FILENAME, ERRORS_FILENAME);
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // displays the error
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • Line 4: Strict adherence to function parameter types is enforced;
  • Line 7: The script [main.php] is also placed in the [Application] namespace;
  • Lines 10–15: The class and interface files used by the script are loaded. Note that here we did not use a [use] statement to declare the full names of the classes used by the script. This is unnecessary because the script and the classes are in the same namespace, [Application]. Also note the loading order: a parent class or interface must be loaded before the class that derives from or implements it;
  • lines 18–21: the names of the files used in the script. These names are relative: the files are searched for in the current directory, the one from which the script is executed;
  • line 25: A [ImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] object is created. This may throw an exception if the JSON file is missing or incorrect;
  • line 27: the [executeBatchImpots] method is called, which will calculate taxes for all taxpayers in the [TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME] file. The results will be written to the file [RESULTS_FILENAME], and any errors will be written to the file [ERRORS_FILENAME];
  • Lines 28–31: If an error occurs, the error code and message are displayed. The expression [{$ex->getCode()}] allows the result of a method call to be inserted into a string.
