docs.title: 8.10. Conclusion
docs.text:
Version 3 has the same functionality as version 2 but is better equipped to handle errors: incomplete or incorrect tax data, erroneous lines in the taxpayer file, or missing files. Each error is flagged by a [ExceptionImpots] exception that includes a message and a specific code.

However, the [AbstractBaseImpots] class combines two types of codes: tax calculation on the one hand, and reading and writing files on the other. In the following chapters, we will see how to separate these two concerns into different layers.

docs.title: 13. Practical Exercise – Version 5
docs.text:
We have already written several versions of this exercise. The latest version used a layered architecture:

The [dao] layer implements the [InterfaceDao] interface. We created a class that implements this interface:

  • [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile], which retrieved tax data from a file named JSON.

We will implement the [InterfaceDao] interface using a new class, [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase], which will retrieve data from the tax authority from a database named MySQL.

docs.title: 13.1. Creating the [dbimpots-2019] database
docs.text:
Following the example from the previous chapter, we will create a MySQL database named [dbimpots-2019], owned by the user [admimpots] with the password [mdpimpots]. This database will have two tables:

  • the table [tbtranches] will contain the tax brackets;
  • the table [tbconstantes] will contain the constants used in tax calculation.

Course PHP 7 created the database, the user, and the tables using the [phpMyAdmin] wizard, then exported the resulting structure to a SQL file. We’ll take the reverse approach: we’ll write the script SQL [dbimpots-2019.sql] directly, placing it in the [Data] folder of version 5:

-- database [dbimpots-2019] of the tax calculation application - SGBD MySQL
-- to be run by the administrator [root] of SGBD:
--    mysql -u root < dbimpots-2019.sql
-- The database, its tables, and its user are recreated if they already exist

-- the database
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS `dbimpots-2019`;
CREATE DATABASE `dbimpots-2019` CHARACTER SET utf8mb4;

-- its owner [admimpots] and password [mdpimpots]
DROP USER IF EXISTS 'admimpots'@'localhost';
CREATE USER 'admimpots'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY 'mdpimpots';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON `dbimpots-2019`.* TO 'admimpots'@'localhost';

-- the tables are created in the database [dbimpots-2019]
USE `dbimpots-2019`;

-- the tax bracket table
CREATE TABLE tbtranches (
    id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    limites DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    coeffr DECIMAL(6, 2) NOT NULL,
    coeffn DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)
);

-- the tax calculation constants table
CREATE TABLE tbconstantes (
    id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
    plafondQfDemiPart DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    valeurReducDemiPart DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondDecoteCelibataire DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondDecoteCouple DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    plafondImpotCouplePourDecote DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    abattementDixPourcentMax DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    abattementDixPourcentMin DECIMAL(10, 2) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)
);

Comments

  • Line 7: The [dbimpots-2019] database is deleted if it exists. The script can then be run again to regenerate the database if it has been deleted or corrupted. The database name contains a hyphen: it must be enclosed in backquotes ` so that MySQL does not interpret it as a subtraction;
  • line 8: create the database with the character set [utf8mb4];
  • lines 11–13: The user [admimpots], with password [mdpimpots], is (re)created. This user has full privileges on the database [dbimpots-2019];
  • line 16: the following commands apply to the database [dbimpots-2019];
  • Lines 19–25: The table [tbtranches] has four columns:
    • [id] is an integer, the table’s primary key, and will be auto-incremented by SGBD ([AUTO_INCREMENT]). This means that MySQL will manage the primary key values itself during inserts: it will assign the value 1 to the primary key of the first insert, then 2 to the next one, and so on;
    • [limites] is a 10-digit decimal number with 2 decimal places ([DECIMAL(10, 2)]). It will contain the elements from the [limites] column of the tax brackets;
    • [coeffr] is a 6-digit decimal number with 2 decimal places. It will contain the elements from column [coeffR] of the tax brackets;
    • [coeffn] is a 10-digit decimal number with 2 decimal places. It will contain the elements from column [coeffN] of the tax brackets;
  • Rows 28–41: Table [tbconstantes] has a primary key [id] and one decimal column per tax calculation constant. It will contain only one row.

The type [DECIMAL] stores numbers exactly, unlike the real types [FLOAT] and [DOUBLE], which store an approximated value in binary: 0.14 is stored exactly as 0.14.

Run this script in the [Laragon] terminal opened in the [version-05/Data] folder using the command:

mysql -u root < dbimpots-2019.sql

If everything goes well, nothing is displayed. Verify the result by logging in as [admimpots]:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "show tables"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+-------------------------+
| Tables_in_dbimpots-2019 |
+-------------------------+
| tbconstantes            |
| tbtranches              |
+-------------------------+

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "describe tbtranches"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
| Field   | Type          | Null | Key | Default | Extra          |
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
| id      | int           | NO   | PRI | NULL    | auto_increment |
| limites | decimal(10,2) | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
| coeffr  | decimal(6,2)  | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
| coeffn  | decimal(10,2) | NO   |     | NULL    |                |
+---------+---------------+------+-----+---------+----------------+
  • Line 6: The [id] column is the primary key (PRI), and its values are managed by MySQL (auto_increment).

Of course, you can also open and run the script [dbimpots-2019.sql] in [HeidiSQL] or [phpMyAdmin] to examine the table structure there.

docs.title: 13.2. Code Organization
docs.text:
To better illustrate the role of the various PHP scripts we are writing, we will organize the code for Version 5 into folders:

version-05
├── Dao
│   ├── DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php
│   ├── DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php
│   ├── InterfaceDao.php
│   ├── InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php
│   └── TraitDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── database.json
│   ├── dbimpots-2019.sql
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── resultats.json
│   ├── taxadmindata.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Entities
│   ├── Database.php
│   ├── ExceptionImpots.php
│   ├── TaxAdminData.php
│   └── TaxPayerData.php
├── Main
│   ├── MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInMySQLDatabase.php
│   └── MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php
├── Metier
│   ├── InterfaceMetier.php
│   └── Metier.php
├── Tests
│   ├── data
│   │   ├── database-incomplet.json
│   │   └── database-mdp-errone.json
│   ├── DaoTest.php
│   └── MetierTest.php
└── Utilities
    └── Utilitaires.php
  • [Entities]: application entities, objects exchanged between layers;
  • [Utilities]: application utilities;
  • [Data]: data used or produced by the application, and the database script SQL. Here, we have decided to use only JSON files for text files. These offer several advantages:
    • they are recognized by many tools;
    • these tools support syntax highlighting. Furthermore, the JSON notation follows specific rules. When these rules are not followed, the tools flag the error. For example, a mistake that is difficult to detect in a basic text file is using the uppercase letter O instead of the number zero. If, in the file JSON, you inadvertently type ["plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42O74], [VS Code] underlines the value 42O74 in red—since it is neither a number nor a string enclosed in quotes—and the [Problèmes] tab displays the error. The developer’s attention is drawn to the error, and they can correct it;
  • [Dao]: the interfaces, traits, and classes of the [dao] layer;
  • [Metier]: the interface and class of the [métier] layer. Course PHP 7 referred to this folder as [Métier]. We avoid accented characters in folder and file names: they cause problems when files are transferred from one system to another (ZIP archives, Git repositories, etc.);
  • [Main]: the main scripts for version 5;
  • [Tests]: the tests for version 5 ([PHPUnit]).

Version 5 has two distinct objectives:

  • to populate the database MySQL [dbimpots-2019] with the contents of the file JSON [Data/taxadmindata.json];
  • to implement tax calculation using tax data that now comes from the MySQL and [dbimpots-2019] databases.

We will address these two objectives separately.

docs.title: 13.3.1. Objective
docs.text:
The file [Data/taxadmindata.json] contains data from the tax authority. This is the version 4 file:

{
    "limites": [9964, 27519, 73779, 156244, 0],
    "coeffR": [0, 0.14, 0.3, 0.41, 0.45],
    "coeffN": [0, 1394.96, 5798, 13913.69, 20163.45],
    "plafondQfDemiPart": 1551,
    "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": 21037,
    "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": 42074,
    "valeurReducDemiPart": 3797,
    "plafondDecoteCelibataire": 1196,
    "plafondDecoteCouple": 1970,
    "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote": 2627,
    "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": 1595,
    "abattementDixPourcentMax": 12502,
    "abattementDixPourcentMin": 437
}

Our objective is to transfer this data to the MySQL and [dbimpots-2019] databases created earlier.

docs.title: 13.3.2. Entities
docs.text:
Entities are the objects exchanged between the application layers. Three of them come from version 4 and are included without any modifications:

  • the exception [ExceptionImpots];
  • the [readonly] [TaxAdminData] class containing tax administration data, constructed using its static methods [fromJsonFile] and [fromArray];
  • the class [readonly] [TaxPayerData] containing a taxpayer’s data and the results of their tax calculation.

We are adding a fourth one, the entity [Database], which describes the database.

docs.title: 13.3.2.1. Why is there no base class [BaseEntity]?
docs.text:
Course PHP 7 introduced a parent class, [BaseEntity], at this point, from which all entities were derived. It was based on a rule: the attributes of an entity have the same names as the keys in the JSON file that it encapsulates. [BaseEntity] was then able to initialize any entity from a JSON file or an associative array using the following loop:

foreach ($arrayOfAttributes as $key => $value) {
  $this->$key = $value;
}

The entity attributes were declared as [protected] (untyped) so that the parent class could modify them, and each entity added its own getters and setters. We are not adopting this solution:

  • the loop above silently creates a dynamic attribute when a key in the JSON file is misspelled. This has been deprecated since PHP 8.2, and is prohibited for [readonly] classes;
  • Entities could be modified by any layer, via their setters or the [setFromArrayOfAttributes] method. Our entities are immutable: a layer cannot accidentally modify an object it received from another layer;
  • the rule “same names in JSON and in the class” still applies, but PHP 8 uses it directly: the expression [new self(...$tableau)] converts the array keys into named arguments for the constructor (PHP 8.1). It is PHP that then verifies that no keys are missing, that none are unknown, and that each value is of the correct type. There is no longer any common code to factor out into a parent class.

Finally, version 4 has already added the [fromArray] method to the [TaxAdminData] class. We will see that this method is sufficient to construct a [TaxAdminData] object from the data read from the database. An important consequence is that the [métier] layer from version 4 will be reused without modification: in course PHP 7, changes to the entities had required modifying the [métier] layer.

docs.title: 13.3.2.2. The entity [Database]
docs.text:
The entity [Database] will be used to encapsulate the data from the following file: JSON [Data/database.json]:

{
    "dsn": "mysql:host=localhost;dbname=dbimpots-2019;charset=utf8mb4",
    "id": "admimpots",
    "pwd": "mdpimpots",
    "tableTranches": "tbtranches",
    "colId": "id",
    "colLimites": "limites",
    "colCoeffR": "coeffr",
    "colCoeffN": "coeffn",
    "tableConstantes": "tbconstantes",
    "colPlafondQfDemiPart": "plafondQfDemiPart",
    "colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction": "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
    "colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction": "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
    "colValeurReducDemiPart": "valeurReducDemiPart",
    "colPlafondDecoteCelibataire": "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
    "colPlafondDecoteCouple": "plafondDecoteCouple",
    "colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote": "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
    "colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote": "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
    "colAbattementDixPourcentMax": "abattementDixPourcentMax",
    "colAbattementDixPourcentMin": "abattementDixPourcentMin"
}

Its attributes describe the characteristics of the MySQL and [dbimpots-2019] databases:

AttributeRoledsnThe DSN databaseidthe database ownerpwdtheir passwordtableTranchesthe name of the table containing the tax bracketscolId / colLimites / colCoeffR / colCoeffNthe column names in the table [tableTranches]tableConstantesthe name of the table containing the tax calculation constantscolPlafondQfDemiPart / colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction / colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction / colValeurReducDemiPart / colPlafondDecoteCelibataire / colPlafondDecoteCouple / colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote / colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote / colAbattementDixPourcentMax / colAbattementDixPourcentMinthe column names in table [tableConstantes] containing the tax calculation constants

Why list the table and column names when we already know them and they’re not likely to change? After SGBD and MySQL, we will use SGBD and PostgreSQL to store tax administration data. However, the column and table names in PostgreSQL do not follow the same rules as those in MySQL. We will have to use different names. This also applies to other SGBD tables. If we want the code to be portable across SGBD tables, it is preferable to use parameters rather than hard-coded table and column names. Compared to course PHP 7, we have added the attribute [colId], which is the name of the primary key column in the slice table: we’ll need this to read the slices back in the order in which they were inserted.

The [Database] class is as follows: [Entities/Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the description of the tax data database: an immutable object
final readonly class Database
{
     // tax calculation constants: each has its own column in the table [tableConstantes]
    public const array CONSTANTES = [
        "plafondQfDemiPart",
        "plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction",
        "plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction",
        "valeurReducDemiPart",
        "plafondDecoteCelibataire",
        "plafondDecoteCouple",
        "plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote",
        "plafondImpotCouplePourDecote",
        "abattementDixPourcentMax",
        "abattementDixPourcentMin",
    ];

     // Private constructor: You must use the [fromJsonFile] method
    private function __construct(
         // connection to the database
        public string $dsn,
        public string $id,
         #[\SensitiveParameter] public string $pwd,
         // the tax bracket table and its columns
        public string $tableTranches,
        public string $colId,
        public string $colLimites,
        public string $colCoeffR,
        public string $colCoeffN,
         // the calculation constants table and its columns
        public string $tableConstantes,
        public string $colPlafondQfDemiPart,
        public string $colPlafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction,
        public string $colPlafondRevenusCouplePourReduction,
        public string $colValeurReducDemiPart,
        public string $colPlafondDecoteCelibataire,
        public string $colPlafondDecoteCouple,
        public string $colPlafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote,
        public string $colPlafondImpotCouplePourDecote,
        public string $colAbattementDixPourcentMax,
        public string $colAbattementDixPourcentMin,
    ) {
    }

     // construction from a file JSON whose keys are the attribute names
    public static function fromJsonFile(string $databaseFilename): self
    {
         // may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $data = Utilitaires::lireFichierJson($databaseFilename);
         // JSON must be an object {...}
        if (!is_array($data) || array_is_list($data)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$databaseFilename] ne contient pas un objet JSON", 20);
        }
        try {
             // the array keys become named arguments for the constructor
            return new self(...$data);
        } catch (\Error $ex) {
             // unknown key, missing key, value that is not a string...
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$databaseFilename] est incorrect ({$ex->getMessage()})", 21, $ex);
        }
    }

     // the column names of the calculation constants: [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
    public function colonnesConstantes(): array
    {
        $colonnes = [];
        foreach (self::CONSTANTES as $constante) {
             // the column for the constant [plafondQfDemiPart] is in the attribute [colPlafondQfDemiPart]
            $colonnes[$constante] = $this->{"col" . ucfirst($constante)};
        }
        return $colonnes;
    }
}

Comments

  • Line 9: Like [TaxAdminData], the class [Database] is immutable and cannot be derived;
  • lines 12–23: the names of the ten tax calculation constants. These are also the names of the attributes of the [TaxAdminData] class;
  • lines 26–50: the private constructor declares, by promotion, a public attribute of type [string] for each key in the [database.json] file, with the same name;
  • line 30: The attribute PHP 8.2 [#[\SensitiveParameter]] marks the parameter as sensitive. If an exception is thrown while the constructor is executing, the password value will not appear in the exception’s call stack (stack trace), which is often written to log files: it is replaced there by a [SensitiveParameterValue] object;
  • lines 53–68: the static method [fromJsonFile] constructs a [Database] object from a JSON file:
    • line 56: reading and decoding the JSON file are handled by the [Utilitaires] class, described later. These operations may throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception;
    • line 58: JSON must be an object—that is, an associative array, not a list;
    • line 63: the keys of the [$data] array become named arguments of the constructor. If a key is missing, PHP throws a [ArgumentCountError] error; if a key is unknown, an error [Error] (“Unknown named parameter”); if a value is not a string, an error [TypeError]. These three errors are derived from the class [Error];
    • Lines 64–66: The error is caught and converted to [ExceptionImpots] with code 21, while retaining the original error ([$ex]) as the preceding exception. The error message for PHP, included in the message, specifies exactly what is wrong;
  • lines 71–79: the method [colonnesConstantes] returns the associative array [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]. For the constant [plafondQfDemiPart], the column name is in the attribute [colPlafondQfDemiPart]. The function [ucfirst] capitalizes the first letter of a string, and the syntax [$this->{"col" . ucfirst($constante)}] refers to the attribute whose name is the value of the expression within the curly braces. This method will save us from having to write nearly identical code ten times in the [dao] layer.

docs.title: 13.3.2.3. The [Utilitaires] class
docs.text:
Version 4 used the [Utilitaires] class to remove the line-end character from the lines of a text file. We now only use JSON files: the [Utilitaires] class now handles both reading and writing JSON and [Utilities/Utilitaires.php] files:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// a utility class: it is neither instantiable nor derivable
final class Utilitaires
{
     // private constructor: the class cannot be instantiated
    private function __construct()
    {
    }

     // reads a JSON file and returns its decoded content (JSON objects become associative arrays)
    public static function lireFichierJson(string $fileName): mixed
    {
         // retrieves the file’s contents
        $contenu = is_readable($fileName) ? file_get_contents($fileName) : false;
        if ($contenu === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$fileName] n'existe pas ou ne peut être lu", 15);
        }
         // decodes the JSON
        try {
            return json_decode($contenu, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$fileName] ne contient pas du JSON valide ({$ex->getMessage()})", 16, $ex);
        }
    }

     // saves a value in JSON format to a text file (created if it doesn’t exist, overwritten otherwise)
    public static function écrireFichierJson(string $fileName, mixed $data): void
    {
         // Indented JSON, unescaped accented characters, real numbers always written with a decimal point (0.0)
        $json = json_encode($data, JSON_PRETTY_PRINT | JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
        if (@file_put_contents($fileName, "$json\n") === false) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur lors de l'enregistrement de données dans le fichier [$fileName]", 14);
        }
    }
}

Comments

  • Lines 17–30: The [lireFichierJson] method reads a JSON file and returns its decoded content, which can be of any type ([mixed]): A JSON object returns an associative array, while a JSON array returns a list. The code is the one we wrote in the [TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile] method in version 3. Errors are reported by a [ExceptionImpots] with code 15 (unreadable file) or 16 (invalid JSON);
  • lines 33–40: the [écrireFichierJson] method writes a value in JSON format to a text file. The [json_encode] options are combined by the [|] operator:
    • [JSON_PRETTY_PRINT] produces an indented, easy-to-read JSON;
    • [JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE] writes accented characters as they appear (marié) instead of their code (mari\u00e9);
    • [JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION] writes the real number 0.0 as 0.0 rather than 0: this distinguishes real numbers from integers in the output file;
    • [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] triggers a [JsonException] exception if the value cannot be encoded in JSON.

docs.title: 13.3.3. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
Now we can write the code that will transfer the data from the JSON and [taxadmindata.json] files into the [tbtranches, tbconstantes] tables in the MySQL and [dbimpots-2019]. We will use the following architecture:

The [dao] layer will implement the following [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface: [Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the interface of the [dao] layer for transferring tax data to a database
interface InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database
{
     // saves tax authority data to the database
     // throws a [ExceptionImpots] exception in case of an error
    public function transferAdminData2Database(): void;
}
  • Line 13: The [transferAdminData2Database] method is responsible for storing tax administration data in a database.

The [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface will be implemented by the following [DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database] class: [Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// transfers tax authority data from a JSON file to a database
class DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database implements InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database
{
     // Description of the target database
    private readonly Database $database;
     // Tax authority data
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

     // The builder
    public function __construct(string $databaseFilename, string $taxAdminDataFilename)
    {
         // may trigger an exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $this->database = Database::fromJsonFile($databaseFilename);
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile($taxAdminDataFilename);
    }

     // transfers tax data to the database
     #[\Override]
    public function transferAdminData2Database(): void
    {
        $database = $this->database;
        try {
             // opens the connection to the database
            $connexion = \PDO::connect($database->dsn, $database->id, $database->pwd);
             // a transaction is started
            $connexion->beginTransaction();
             // Fill in the tax bracket table
            $this->fillTableTranches($connexion);
             // Fill the constants table
            $this->fillTableConstantes($connexion);
             // The transaction is successfully completed
            $connexion->commit();
        } catch (\PDOException $ex) {
             // Is there a transaction in progress?
            if (isset($connexion) && $connexion->inTransaction()) {
                 // The transaction is terminated due to a failure
                $connexion->rollBack();
            }
             // The error is propagated to the calling code as an exception [ExceptionImpots]
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur d'accès à la base de données ({$ex->getMessage()})", 30, $ex);
        }
         // The connection is closed when the variable [$connexion] is no longer present, at the end of the method
    }

Comments

Here, we are applying what we learned in the chapter on MySQL.

  • Line 9: The [DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database] class implements the [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface;
  • line 12: the attribute [$database] is an object of type [Database] that encapsulates the data from the file [database.json];
  • line 14: the attribute [$taxAdminData] is an object of type [TaxAdminData] that encapsulates the data from the file [taxadmindata.json];
  • lines 17–22: The constructor takes the names of the [database.json, taxadmindata.json] files as parameters and initializes the two attributes. If one of the files is invalid, a [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown to the calling code;
  • line 26: the single method of the [InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database] interface is implemented;
  • line 31: the database connection is opened. Note the notation [\PDO], which refers to the class [PDO] of PHP. In fact, since we are in the [Application] namespace, if we simply wrote [PDO], this relative name would be prefixed with the current namespace and would therefore refer to the class [Application\PDO], which does not exist. The method [PDO::connect] returns an object of type [Pdo\Mysql] here, since DSN begins with [mysql:]. Nothing in this class depends on MySQL: it is DSN—read from the [database.json] file—that determines the SGBD used;
  • Lines 33–39: The [tbtranches, tbconstantes] tables are populated within a transaction. The methods [fillTableTranches] and [fillTableConstantes] trigger a [PDOException] as soon as something goes wrong. In this case, execution continues in the [catch] clause, and the database remains in its initial state: there is no risk of having a filled [tbtranches] table and an empty [tbconstantes] table;
  • Lines 40–47: Case where an exception was thrown by the code. If a transaction is in progress, it is rolled back. Then an exception of type [ExceptionImpots], with code 30, is thrown, along with the message from the original exception, which becomes the preceding exception. The calling code thus only has to handle one exception type;
  • line 49: the PHP 7 procedure closed the connection within a [finally] clause using the [$connexion = NULL] statement. This is unnecessary: the local variable [$connexion] disappears at the end of the method, and with it, the connection.

The code for the [fillTableTranches] method is as follows:

     // Filling in the tax bracket table
    private function fillTableTranches(\PDO $connexion): void
    {
         // shortcuts
        $database = $this->database;
        $taxAdminData = $this->taxAdminData;
         // The table is cleared in case it contains any data
        $connexion->exec("delete from $database->tableTranches");
         // Prepare the inserts
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "insert into $database->tableTranches ($database->colLimites, $database->colCoeffR, $database->colCoeffN)"
            . " values (:limites, :coeffR, :coeffN)"
        );
         // execute the prepared command with the values for each tax bracket
        foreach ($taxAdminData->limites as $i => $limite) {
            $statement->execute([
                "limites" => $limite,
                "coeffR" => $taxAdminData->coeffR[$i],
                "coeffN" => $taxAdminData->coeffN[$i],
            ]);
        }
    }

Comments

  • Line 53: The [fillTableTranches] method receives an open connection as a parameter. We also know that a transaction has started within this connection;
  • Lines 56–57: Two shortcuts to avoid having to write [$this->database] and [$this->taxAdminData] throughout the code. These are copies of object references, not copies of the objects themselves;
  • line 59: the current contents of the "tranches" table are deleted. The table name is inserted into the string using the syntax ["$database->tableTranches"]: PHP replaces the expression with the value of the attribute;
  • Lines 61–64: The insertion of rows into the table is prepared. Here, the table and column names provided by the attribute [$database] are used. Table and column names cannot be parameters of a prepared statement; only values can be. This is why they are inserted into the text of the SQL statement. They come from a configuration file and not from a user: there is no risk of SQL injection;
  • Lines 66–72: The prepared insertion statement is executed as many times as necessary, once per tax bracket. [$i] is the bracket number, which serves as an index in the tables [coeffR] and [coeffN].

The method code for [fillTableConstantes] is as follows:

     // Fill the constants table
    private function fillTableConstantes(\PDO $connexion): void
    {
         // shortcut
        $database = $this->database;
         // Clearing the table in case it contains anything
        $connexion->exec("delete from $database->tableConstantes");
         // [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
        $colonnes = $database->colonnesConstantes();
         // The parameters of the prepared order are named after constants: :plafondQfDemiPart, ...
        $paramètres = array_map(fn(string $constante): string => ":$constante", array_keys($colonnes));
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "insert into $database->tableConstantes (" . implode(", ", $colonnes) . ")"
            . " values (" . implode(", ", $paramètres) . ")"
        );
         // the parameter values: [nom de la constante => valeur de la constante]
        $valeurs = [];
        foreach (array_keys($colonnes) as $constante) {
            $valeurs[$constante] = $this->taxAdminData->$constante;
        }
         // the prepared statement is executed: a single row is inserted
        $statement->execute($valeurs);
    }

Comments

  • Line 76: The method [fillTableConstantes] also receives an open connection in which a transaction is in progress;
  • Line 81: The table [tbconstantes] is cleared;
  • line 83: the array [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne], for example, [["plafondQfDemiPart" => "plafondQfDemiPart", ...]];
  • line 85: the names of the parameters for the prepared statement: [[":plafondQfDemiPart", ...]]. These are the names of the constants preceded by a colon;
  • lines 86–89: preparation of the insertion command SQL. The function [implode] constructs the list of columns and the list of parameters, separated by commas. This results in the command [insert into tbconstantes (plafondQfDemiPart, ...) values (:plafondQfDemiPart, ...)]. Course PHP 7 wrote this entire command, column by column, over about twenty lines;
  • lines 91–94: the table of parameter values for [nom de la constante => valeur]. The syntax [$this->taxAdminData->$constante] specifies the attribute of the object [TaxAdminData], whose name is the value of the variable [$constante];
  • Line 96: Execution of the insert statement. There is only one row to insert.

docs.title: 13.3.4. The main script
docs.text:
The main script [Main/MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php] relies on the layer [dao] to perform the data transfer:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Inclusion of the interfaces and classes required for the transfer
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php";

// Definition of constants
const DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/database.json";
const TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/taxadmindata.json";

try {
     // Creation of the layer [dao]
    $dao = new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database(DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME, TAXADMINDATA_FILENAME);
     // Data transfer to the database
    $dao->transferAdminData2Database();
    print "Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base de données\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // error displayed
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • Lines 10–15: Load the classes and interfaces required for the transfer. The paths are relative to the script’s folder ([Main]): [__DIR__ . "/../Entities"] refers to the adjacent folder [Entities];
  • Lines 18–19: The paths to the two JSON files, which are also relative to the script folder. Course PHP 7 used paths relative to the current folder (["../Data/database.json"]): the script only worked if it was run from the [Main] folder;
  • line 23: the [dao] layer is instantiated by passing the names of the two JSON files to the constructor;
  • line 25: the data transfer is performed;
  • lines 27–29: the exception code and message are displayed. Course PHP 7 used the function [utf8_encode] here, which has been deprecated since PHP 8.2 and is unnecessary since all our messages are in UTF-8.

When we run this script in a terminal opened in the [Main] folder, we get the following result:

> php MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2MySQLDatabase.php
Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base de données
Terminé

and the following content in the database:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "select * from tbtranches"
mysql: [Warning] Using a password on the command line interface can be insecure.
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
| id | limites   | coeffr | coeffn   |
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
|  1 |   9964.00 |   0.00 |     0.00 |
|  2 |  27519.00 |   0.14 |  1394.96 |
|  3 |  73779.00 |   0.30 |  5798.00 |
|  4 | 156244.00 |   0.41 | 13913.69 |
|  5 |      0.00 |   0.45 | 20163.45 |
+----+-----------+--------+----------+
  • column [id]: the values assigned by MySQL to the primary key. Numbering starts at 1. If we run the script again, the rows are deleted and then reinserted, and MySQL continues the numbering (6, 7…): an auto-increment key value is never reused;
  • the numbers have two decimal places, in accordance with the [DECIMAL(10, 2)] data type of the columns.

The option [\G] at the end of the SQL command displays each row vertically, one column per screen line, which is easier to read for a table with many columns:

> mysql -u admimpots -pmdpimpots dbimpots-2019 -e "select * from tbconstantes\G"

docs.title: 13.4.1. Architecture
docs.text:
Version 4 of the tax calculation application used a layered architecture:

The [dao] layer implements the [InterfaceDao] interface. The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInJsonFile] class in version 4 retrieved tax data from a JSON file. We will implement the [InterfaceDao] interface using a new class, [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase], which will retrieve data from the tax authority from the MySQL database. The [dao] layer, as before, will write the results and errors to text files and retrieve taxpayer data from a text file as well. Only this time, these text files will be JSON files. Furthermore, we know that if we continue to adhere to the [InterfaceDao] interface, the [métier] layer will not need to be modified.

docs.title: 13.4.2. The [TaxPayerData] entity
docs.text:
The [TaxPayerData] class in version 4 encapsulates the data for a taxpayer ([marié, enfants, salaire]) and the results of their tax calculation ([impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]). It is carried over as-is. The taxpayer data is now in the following JSON and [Data/taxpayersdata.json] files:

The keys for the JSON objects are the names of the attributes in the [TaxPayerData] class. Note the following:

  • line 8: taxpayer #1 (numbers start at 0) is incorrect: all three of their data entries are invalid;
  • line 14: the number of children for taxpayer No. 2 is given as a string. We will accept it;
  • the other eleven taxpayers are those from the tax administration’s official tests, which have been used since version 1.

docs.title: 13.4.3.1. The [InterfaceDao] interface
docs.text:
The [InterfaceDao] interface from version 4 is included without modification [Dao/InterfaceDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// [dao] layer interface
// All methods throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception in the event of an unrecoverable error
interface InterfaceDao
{
     // Reading taxpayer data
     // Erroneous rows are flagged in the text file [$errorsFilename]
     /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

     // Reading data from the tax authority (tax brackets and constants)
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;

     // saving the results
     /** @param TaxPayerData[] $taxPayersData */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void;
}

The methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] accept filenames: there is no indication that these are basic text files or JSON files. The interface therefore remains valid.

docs.title: 13.4.3.2. The feature [TraitDao]
docs.text:
The [TraitDao] trait implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods of the [InterfaceDao] interface. Since we’ve switched from basic text files to JSON files, we need to rewrite it as [Dao/TraitDao.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Implementation of methods from [InterfaceDao] that work with JSON files
trait TraitDao
{
     // Reading taxpayer data from a file JSON
     #[\Override]
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array
    {
         // the file contents: an array of objects {spouse, children, salary}
         // may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $contribuables = Utilitaires::lireFichierJson($taxPayersFilename);
        if (!is_array($contribuables) || !array_is_list($contribuables)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Le fichier [$taxPayersFilename] ne contient pas un tableau JSON", 17);
        }
         // array of taxpayer data
        $taxPayersData = [];
         // array of errors
        $errors = [];
         // Each taxpayer is verified
        foreach ($contribuables as $numéro => $contribuable) {
            $erreurs = $this->check($contribuable);
            if ($erreurs === []) {
                 // one more taxpayer
                $taxPayersData[] = new TaxPayerData(
                    strtolower(trim($contribuable["marié"])),
                    (int) $contribuable["enfants"],
                    (int) $contribuable["salaire"]
                );
            } else {
                 // one more error: the number of the erroneous taxpayer is recorded in the table JSON
                $errors[] = ["numéro" => $numéro, "erreurs" => $erreurs];
            }
        }
         // The errors are saved to a file named JSON
        Utilitaires::écrireFichierJson($errorsFilename, $errors);
         // Result of the function
        return $taxPayersData;
    }

     // Verification of a taxpayer’s data: returns a list of incorrect attributes
    private function check(mixed $contribuable): array
    {
         // The taxpayer must be an object JSON
        if (!is_array($contribuable)) {
            return [["contribuable" => $contribuable]];
        }
        $erreurs = [];
         // Marital status must be "yes" or "no"
        $marié = $contribuable["marié"] ?? null;
        if (!is_string($marié) || !in_array(strtolower(trim($marié)), ["oui", "non"], true)) {
            $erreurs[] = ["marié" => $marié];
        }
         // The number of children and the salary must be positive integers or zero
         // specified as a number (2) or a string ("2")
        foreach (["enfants", "salaire"] as $clé) {
            $valeur = $contribuable[$clé] ?? null;
            $valide = (is_int($valeur) && $valeur >= 0)
                || (is_string($valeur) && preg_match('/^\s*\d+\s*$/', $valeur) === 1);
            if (!$valide) {
                $erreurs[] = [$clé => $valeur];
            }
        }
        return $erreurs;
    }

     // Save results to a file JSON
     #[\Override]
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void
    {
         // [TaxPayerData] objects are converted to JSON objects based on their public attributes
        Utilitaires::écrireFichierJson($resultsFilename, $taxPayersData);
    }
}

Comments

  • Lines 13–44: The [getTaxPayersData] method takes the following parameters:
    • [$taxPayersFilename]: the name of the JSON file containing taxpayer data [taxpayersdata.json];
    • [$errorsFilename]: the name of the JSON file containing the [errors.json] errors;
  • Line 17: The contents of the JSON file containing taxpayer data are decoded into the [$contribuables] table. If the file JSON proves to be unusable, a [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown;
  • line 18: the content must be a JSON array, i.e., a PHP list. Otherwise, a code 17 exception is thrown;
  • line 22: the array [$taxPayersData] will contain taxpayer data encapsulated in objects of type [TaxPayerData];
  • line 24: errors will be accumulated in the array [$errors];
  • lines 26–39: construction of the array [$taxPayersData]. Before being encapsulated in a [TaxPayerData] object, the data is validated by the [check] method, which returns a list of invalid attributes—or an empty list if the data is valid:
    • Lines 30–34: Case where the data is valid. A new [TaxPayerData] object is created and added to the [$taxPayersData] array. The marital status is converted to lowercase, and the number of children and the salary are converted to integers: [(int) "2"] is set to 2;
    • Line 37: Cases where the data is invalid. The error message includes the number of the incorrect taxpayer in table JSON so that the user can locate it, and then the error is added to table [$errors];
  • Line 41: The errors encountered are logged in the JSON and [$errorsFilename] files. The PHP 7 course was incorrectly writing a string JSON, one per line: with multiple errors, the file was not a valid JSON file. We write an array JSON of the errors;
  • line 43: we return the array of constructed [TaxPayerData] objects: this was the method’s purpose;
  • lines 47–70: the private method [check] verifies the validity of a taxpayer’s data. The parameter [$contribuable] is of type [mixed]: an element of the array JSON can be anything (an object, a number, a string, etc.). The method aggregates the invalid attributes into the [$erreurs] table in the form of [attribut erroné => valeur] tables:
    • line 50: the element must be an object JSON;
    • line 55: the [??] operator (null coalescing) returns the value of [$contribuable["marié"]] if it exists and is not [null], and [null] otherwise. This avoids the warning that would be triggered by a missing key;
    • lines 56–58: the marital status must be a string representing “yes” or “no,” ignoring case and spaces;
    • lines 61–68: the number of children and the salary must be positive integers or zero, given in the form of a number JSON (2) or a string ("2"). A string must consist of digits, optionally surrounded by spaces: this is what the regular expression [/^\s*\d+\s*$/] checks for. Note the comparison [preg_match(...) === 1]: the function [preg_match] returns 1 if the string matches the pattern, 0 otherwise, and [false] in case of an error;
  • Lines 74–78: the implementation of the [saveResults] method of the [InterfaceDao] interface. The array of [TaxPayerData] objects is directly stored in the JSON format: the function [json_encode] converts an object into a JSON object whose keys are the names of its public attributes. The PHP 7 course constructed the JSON string from the array “by hand,” by concatenating the JSON strings of the objects separated by commas and adding square brackets.

docs.title: 13.4.3.3. The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class
docs.text:
The [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class implements the [InterfaceDao] interface as follows: [Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php]:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// a layer [dao] that retrieves tax administration data from a database
class DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase implements InterfaceDao
{
     // the trait implements the methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] of the interface
    use TraitDao;

     // the database description
    private readonly Database $database;
     // the object of type [TaxAdminData], which contains data from the tax administration
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

     // the constructor
    public function __construct(string $databaseFilename)
    {
         // database description—may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $this->database = Database::fromJsonFile($databaseFilename);
        $database = $this->database;
        try {
             // opens the connection to the database
             // The read rows will be returned as associative arrays [colonne => valeur]
            $connexion = \PDO::connect(
                $database->dsn,
                $database->id,
                $database->pwd,
                [\PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => \PDO::FETCH_ASSOC]
            );
             // Start a transaction
            $connexion->beginTransaction();
             // Read the tax bracket table
            $tranches = $this->getTranches($connexion);
             // the constants table is read
            $constantes = $this->getConstantes($connexion);
             // the transaction is successfully completed
            $connexion->commit();
        } catch (\PDOException $ex) {
             // Is there a transaction in progress?
            if (isset($connexion) && $connexion->inTransaction()) {
                 // End the transaction upon failure
                $connexion->rollBack();
            }
             // The error is propagated to the calling code as an exception [ExceptionImpots]
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur d'accès à la base de données ({$ex->getMessage()})", 30, $ex);
        }
         // constructing the object [TaxAdminData]: the read data is verified
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray([...$tranches, ...$constantes]);
    }

Comments

  • line 6: We retain the namespace already used for the other classes in the application;
  • line 9: the class [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] implements the interface [InterfaceDao];
  • line 12: the [TraitDao] trait is imported. We know that this trait implements part of the interface. The only method left to implement is the [getTaxAdminData] method, which simply returns the private attribute [$taxAdminData]. We can infer that the constructor will need to initialize this attribute. That is its sole purpose;
  • line 20: the constructor receives as its only parameter the filename JSON [database.json], which defines the database MySQL [dbimpots-2019];
  • Line 23: The file JSON is used to create an object of type [Database], which is stored in the attribute [$database]. If the file JSON could not be processed correctly, a [ExceptionImpots] exception is thrown;
  • lines 28–33: the database connection is opened. The fourth parameter sets the default mode for reading rows: associative arrays of type [colonne => valeur];
  • line 35: a transaction is started. This is not strictly necessary because only two SQL commands will be executed, and these commands do not modify the database. However, it is done to isolate the program from other database users: both tables are read in the same state, even if another program modifies them at the same time;
  • Line 37: The tax bracket table [tbtranches] is read using the private method [getTranches]. This method returns the array [["limites" => [...], "coeffR" => [...], "coeffN" => [...]]];
  • line 39: The calculation constants table [tbconstantes] is read by the private method [getConstantes]. It returns the array [nom de la constante => valeur];
  • Line 41: If we reach this line, it means everything went well. We therefore commit the transaction;
  • lines 42–49: If we reach this point, it means an exception has occurred. We therefore roll back the transaction if one was in progress. Then, to ensure consistent exceptions, we rethrow the error as an exception of type [ExceptionImpots] with code 30;
  • line 52: the expression [[...$tranches, ...$constantes]] merges the two associative arrays into a single one, which has exactly the thirteen keys expected by the method [TaxAdminData::fromArray]. This method verifies the data read from the database, just as it verified the data from the JSON file, and converts it to real numbers. Course PHP 7 initialized the [TaxAdminData] object attribute by attribute, with ten calls to setters.

The [getTranches] method is as follows:

     // Reading the tax bracket table
     // returns the array ["limites" => [...], "coeffR" => [...], "coeffN" => [...]]
    private function getTranches(\PDO $connexion): array
    {
         // shortcut
        $database = $this->database;
         // Prepare and then execute the query SELECT
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "select $database->colLimites, $database->colCoeffR, $database->colCoeffN"
            . " from $database->tableTranches order by $database->colId"
        );
        $statement->execute();
         // all rows at once: an array of associative arrays
        $tranches = $statement->fetchAll();
         // Extract each column from the result
        return [
            "limites" => array_column($tranches, $database->colLimites),
            "coeffR" => array_column($tranches, $database->colCoeffR),
            "coeffN" => array_column($tranches, $database->colCoeffN),
        ];
    }

Comments

  • line 57: the method receives as a parameter an open connection in which a transaction is in progress;
  • Lines 62–65: The SELECT statement is prepared and then executed. The [order by] clause on the primary key ensures that the chunks are re-read in the order in which they were inserted. The PHP 7 command did not have this clause and relied on the order in which MySQL returned the rows, which is not guaranteed;
  • line 68: all rows of the result are read at once. This yields an array of associative arrays, for example, [[["limites" => "9964.00", "coeffr" => "0.00", "coeffn" => "0.00"], ...]]. Note that the values in the columns of type [DECIMAL] are returned as character strings: PHP does not have an exact decimal type, and the driver does not convert them to [float], which would result in a loss of precision. The [TaxAdminData::fromArray] method will perform the conversion;
  • Lines 70–74: The function [array_column] extracts a column from an array of associative arrays: [array_column($tranches, "limites")] returns [["9964.00", "27519.00", ...]].

The private method [getConstantes] is as follows:

     // Read the calculation constants table
     // returns the array [nom de la constante => valeur]
    private function getConstantes(\PDO $connexion): array
    {
         // [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne]
        $colonnes = $this->database->colonnesConstantes();
         // We prepare and then execute the query SELECT
        $statement = $connexion->prepare(
            "select " . implode(", ", $colonnes) . " from {$this->database->tableConstantes}"
        );
        $statement->execute();
         // We process the result—only one row here—[false] if the table is empty
        $ligne = $statement->fetch() ?: [];
         // [nom de la constante => valeur de sa colonne] (null if the table is empty)
        return array_map(fn(string $colonne): mixed => $ligne[$colonne] ?? null, $colonnes);
    }

Comments

  • line 82: the array [nom de la constante => nom de la colonne];
  • lines 84–86: the SELECT command for the ten columns is prepared and then executed. Note the curly braces in [{$this->database->tableConstantes}]: without them, PHP would interpret only [$this->database] from the string;
  • Line 89: The table has only one row, read by the [fetch] method. This method returns [false] if there is no row. The operator [?:] returns its left operand if it evaluates to true, and its right operand otherwise: [$ligne] therefore evaluates to an empty array if the table is empty;
  • line 91: for each constant, we look up the value of its column in [$ligne]. The function [array_map], when applied to a single array, preserves its keys: we obtain the array [nom de la constante => valeur]. If the table is empty, all values are [null], and the [TaxAdminData::fromArray] method will report an invalid value.

Note that the class does not depend on SGBD or MySQL. It is the [database.json] file that sets the SGBD used via the DSN in the database.

docs.title: 13.4.4. The [métier] layer
docs.text:
• We have just implemented the [dao] and [3] layers;
  • because we adhered to the [InterfaceDao] interface, the [métier] and [2] layers can remain unchanged. Course PHP 7, however, had to modify it because it had also changed the entities exchanged between the layers: the [executeBatchImpots] method used the setters of the [TaxPayerData] class from version 4, which had been removed. Here, the entities have not changed.

The [InterfaceMetier] interface and the [Metier] class from version 4 are therefore included without any modifications in the [Metier] folder. Recall the [executeBatchImpots] method:

     // Batch tax calculation
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
         // allow exceptions originating from the [dao] layer to be propagated
         // retrieve taxpayer data
        $taxPayersData = $this->dao->getTaxPayersData($taxPayersFileName, $errorsFileName);
         // calculate the tax for each taxpayer
        $results = array_map(
            fn(TaxPayerData $taxPayerData): TaxPayerData => $taxPayerData->avecRésultats(
                $this->calculerImpot($taxPayerData->marié, $taxPayerData->enfants, $taxPayerData->salaire)
            ),
            $taxPayersData
        );
         // Save the results
        $this->dao->saveResults($resultsFileName, $results);
    }
}
  • line 192: the [métier] layer is unaware that taxpayer data now comes from a JSON file: it requests the data from the [dao] layer and receives an array of [TaxPayerData] objects, as in version 4;
  • Line 201: Similarly, she is unaware that the results are saved in the format JSON.

docs.title: 13.4.5. The main script
docs.text:
• We have just implemented the layers [dao], [3], [métier], and [2];
  • we still need to write the main script [1].

The main script [Main/MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInMySQLDatabase.php] is similar to the one in version 4:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function results
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Inclusion of interfaces and classes
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxPayerData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/TraitDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Metier/InterfaceMetier.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Metier/Metier.php";

// Definition of constants
const DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/database.json";
const TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/taxpayersdata.json";
const RESULTS_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/resultats.json";
const ERRORS_FILENAME = __DIR__ . "/../Data/errors.json";

try {
     // Creation of the layer [dao]
    $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(DATABASE_CONFIG_FILENAME);
     // Creation of layer [métier]
    $métier = new Metier($dao);
     // Batch tax calculation
    $métier->executeBatchImpots(TAXPAYERSDATA_FILENAME, RESULTS_FILENAME, ERRORS_FILENAME);
    print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [resultats.json]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // Error displayed
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • lines 10–19: loading all the files needed to calculate the tax;
  • lines 22–25: the names of the various JSON files in the application;
  • line 29: construction of the [dao] layer;
  • line 31: construction of the [métier] layer;

docs.title: 13.5. [PHPUnit] Tests
docs.text: As we did for version 4, we will write [PHPUnit] tests for version 5. They are in the [version-05/Tests] folder.

docs.title: 13.5.1. [dao] Layer Test
docs.text:
The [Tests/DaoTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// Test namespace
namespace Application\Tests;

// the classes being tested
use Application\DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase;
use Application\DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database;
use Application\ExceptionImpots;
use Application\InterfaceDao;
use Application\TaxAdminData;
use Application\TaxPayerData;
// the classes in PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

// Loading classes from the [dao] layer
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/ExceptionImpots.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxAdminData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/TaxPayerData.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Entities/Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Utilities/Utilitaires.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/TraitDao.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php";
require_once __DIR__ . "/../Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php";

final class DaoTest extends TestCase
{
     // Version 5 data folder
    private const string DATA = __DIR__ . "/../Data";
     // the tested layer [dao]
    private InterfaceDao $dao;
     // a temporary file for errors
    private string $errorsFilename;

     // run before each test
     #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
         // creation of the layer [dao]
        $this->dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::DATA . "/database.json");
         // a temporary file
        $this->errorsFilename = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "errors");
    }

     // executed after each test
     #[\Override]
    protected function tearDown(): void
    {
         // deletion of the temporary file
        unlink($this->errorsFilename);
    }

     // tax authority data read from the database
    public function testTaxAdminData(): void
    {
        $taxAdminData = $this->dao->getTaxAdminData();
         // calculation constants
        $this->assertSame(1551.0, $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(21037.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(42074.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(3797.0, $taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(1196.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire);
        $this->assertSame(1970.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple);
        $this->assertSame(1595.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(2627.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCouplePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(12502.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMax);
        $this->assertSame(437.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMin);
         // tax brackets
        $this->assertSame([9964.0, 27519.0, 73779.0, 156244.0, 0.0], $taxAdminData->limites);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 0.14, 0.30, 0.41, 0.45], $taxAdminData->coeffR);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 1394.96, 5798.0, 13913.69, 20163.45], $taxAdminData->coeffN);
    }

     // Transfer of the JSON file to the database, followed by a re-read of the database
    public function testTransfert(): void
    {
         // transfer
        (new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database(self::DATA . "/database.json", self::DATA . "/taxadmindata.json"))
            ->transferAdminData2Database();
         // re-reading the database using a new layer [dao]
        $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::DATA . "/database.json");
         // The database contains the data from the JSON file
        $this->assertEquals(TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile(self::DATA . "/taxadmindata.json"), $dao->getTaxAdminData());
    }

     // incorrect database descriptions
    public static function basesInvalides(): array
    {
         // [nom du fichier, code d'erreur attendu]
        return [
            "fichier inexistant" => ["inexistant.json", 15],
            "clé manquante" => ["database-incomplet.json", 21],
            "mot de passe erroné" => ["database-mdp-errone.json", 30],
        ];
    }

     #[DataProvider("basesInvalides")]
    public function testBasesInvalides(string $fichier, int $code): void
    {
         // An exception is expected: [ExceptionImpots] with a specific code
        $this->expectException(ExceptionImpots::class);
        $this->expectExceptionCode($code);
         // Creating a layer [dao] with an incorrect basic description
        new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(__DIR__ . "/data/$fichier");
    }

     // Taxpayer data read from a file JSON
    public function testTaxPayersData(): void
    {
        $taxPayersData = $this->dao->getTaxPayersData(self::DATA . "/taxpayersdata.json", $this->errorsFilename);
         // 11 correct taxpayers
        $this->assertCount(11, $taxPayersData);
        $this->assertContainsOnlyInstancesOf(TaxPayerData::class, $taxPayersData);
         // the first and last
        $this->assertEquals(new TaxPayerData("oui", 2, 55555), $taxPayersData[0]);
        $this->assertEquals(new TaxPayerData("oui", 3, 200000), $taxPayersData[10]);
         // Taxpayer No. 1 in the file JSON is incorrect
        $erreurs = json_decode(file_get_contents($this->errorsFilename), true);
        $this->assertSame([
            ["numéro" => 1, "erreurs" => [["marié" => "ouix"], ["enfants" => "2x"], ["salaire" => "55555x"]]],
        ], $erreurs);
    }

     // A non-existent taxpayer file
    public function testTaxPayersDataInexistant(): void
    {
        $this->expectException(ExceptionImpots::class);
        $this->expectExceptionCode(15);
        $this->dao->getTaxPayersData(self::DATA . "/inexistant.json", $this->errorsFilename);
    }
}

Comments

  • lines 21–30: definition of the test environment. We load the files for the two [dao] layers from version 5: the transfer layer and the tax calculation layer;
  • lines 43–49: Before each test, we construct the [dao] layer using the [Data/database.json] file, just as the main script does;
  • line 60: The [testTaxAdminData] method is identical to that in version 4. However, this time, the data being tested was read from the database;
  • Lines 81–90: We test the transfer of the JSON file to the database, then read the database again using a new layer, [dao]. The resulting [TaxAdminData] object must be equal ([assertEquals]) to the one constructed from the JSON file. This test assumes that the transfer successfully loaded the data from the file [taxadmindata.json] into the database: it does not modify the data expected by the other tests;
  • lines 93–101: three incorrect database descriptions: a nonexistent file (code 15), a file named [database-incomplet.json] that is missing the key [colCoeffN] (code 21), and a file named [database-mdp-errone.json] with an incorrect password (code 30). The last two files are in the [Tests/data] folder;
  • lines 104–111: we verify that a layer named [dao], created with an incorrect description, throws a [ExceptionImpots] exception with the correct error code;
  • lines 114–128: reading taxpayer data from the JSON file. We verify the number of taxpayers retrieved and the contents of the first and last records, then the exact contents of the error file;
  • Line 131: A nonexistent taxpayer file should trigger a code 15 exception.
