docs.title: 15. Practical Exercise – Version 7
docs.text:
Version 7 builds on version 6 by externalizing the constants used in the main scripts—namely, the names of the data files and the list of PHP files to be loaded—into a configuration file. Like version 6, it contains no new classes and uses those from version 5:

version-07
├── Data
│   ├── config.json
│   ├── database-mysql.json
│   ├── database-pgsql.json
│   ├── errors.json
│   ├── results.json
│   ├── taxadmindata.json
│   └── taxpayersdata.json
├── Main
│   ├── MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php
│   └── MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php
└── Tests
    ├── DaoTest.php
    └── MetierTest.php

The [Data] folder contains the descriptions of the two [dbimpots-2019] databases: the MySQL database from version 5 ([database-mysql.json]) and the PostgreSQL database from version 6 ([database-pgsql.json]). In the latter file, table names are no longer prefixed with the schema [public] (["tableTranches": "tbtranches"]).

docs.title: 15.1. Implementation
docs.text:
The configuration file is the following JSON [Data/config.json] file:

{
    "databaseFilename": "Data/database-pgsql.json",
    "taxAdminDataFilename": "Data/taxadmindata.json",
    "taxPayersDataFilename": "Data/taxpayersdata.json",
    "resultsFilename": "Data/results.json",
    "errorsFilename": "Data/errors.json",
    "dependencies": {
        "ExceptionImpots": "../version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "TaxAdminData": "../version-05/Entities/TaxAdminData.php",
        "TaxPayerData": "../version-05/Entities/TaxPayerData.php",
        "Database": "../version-05/Entities/Database.php",
        "Utilitaires": "../version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "InterfaceDao": "../version-05/Dao/InterfaceDao.php",
        "TraitDao": "../version-05/Dao/TraitDao.php",
        "DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase": "../version-05/Dao/DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php",
        "InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database": "../version-05/Dao/InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database.php",
        "DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database": "../version-05/Dao/DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php",
        "InterfaceMetier": "../version-05/Metier/InterfaceMetier.php",
        "Metier": "../version-05/Metier/Metier.php"
    },
    "dependencies4calculate": [
        "ExceptionImpots",
        "TaxAdminData",
        "TaxPayerData",
        "Database",
        "Utilitaires",
        "InterfaceDao",
        "TraitDao",
        "DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase",
        "InterfaceMetier",
        "Metier"
    ],
    "dependencies4transfer": [
        "ExceptionImpots",
        "TaxAdminData",
        "Database",
        "Utilitaires",
        "InterfaceDao4TransferAdminData2Database",
        "DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database"
    ]
}

In this configuration:

  • lines 2–6: the paths to all JSON files in the application. The database used is PostgreSQL;
  • lines 7–20: the paths to all PHP files in the application, in the form [clé => chemin]. These are the files from version 5;
  • lines 21–32: the dependencies for tax calculation in the form of a list of keys from the [dependencies] dictionary;
  • lines 33–40: the dependencies for transferring data from the JSON and [taxadmindata.json] files to the database, in the same format.

All paths are relative to the [version-07] folder. Course PHP 7 added a key named [rootDirectory] to this file, specifying the absolute path to the version folder on the author’s machine (["C:/Data/st-2019/dev/php7/poly/scripts-console/impots/version-07"]): this had to be modified on each new machine. The scripts now calculate this folder path themselves based on the constant [__DIR__]. The [php8-oct-2026] folder can therefore be placed anywhere.

The script for transferring tax administration data to the database, [Main/MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php], is now as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of function parameters and return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the root directory for version 7: paths to the configuration file are relative to this directory
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// Configuration file path
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json";

// retrieve the configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// Include the dependencies required by the script
foreach ($config["dependencies4transfer"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["dependencies"][$dependency];
}

// paths to the data files
$databaseFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"];
$taxAdminDataFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["taxAdminDataFilename"];

try {
     // creating the layer [dao]
    $dao = new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database($databaseFilename, $taxAdminDataFilename);
     // transfer data to the database
    $dao->transferAdminData2Database();
    print "Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base décrite par [{$config["databaseFilename"]}]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // Display the error
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

The code remains the same as in version 6. The only difference is the use of the file [config.json] instead of the constants:

  • Line 10: The root directory for version 7, relative to which the paths in the configuration file are measured. [__DIR__] is the [Main] folder of the script; [__DIR__ . "/.."] is its parent folder, [version-07];
  • line 12: the path to the configuration file;
  • line 15: the function [file_get_contents] converts the file [config.json] into a string. The function [json_decode] then uses this string to construct the associative array [$config]. The second parameter, [true], of the function [json_decode] specifies that an associative array is desired rather than an object. With the [JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR] option, a syntax error in the file triggers a [JsonException] exception. We do not attempt to handle configuration file read errors here: this file is part of the application, and an error at this level is a programming error that PHP reports itself. Data errors (JSON data files, database) are always reported by a [ExceptionImpots];
  • lines 18–20: the dependencies required by the transfer script are included:
    • [$config["dependencies4transfer"]] is the table of dependencies required by the transfer script. It is a list of keys;
    • the paths to the files to be included are found in the dictionary [$config["dependencies"]] and are prefixed with the root directory. For example, the key [ExceptionImpots] refers to the file [version-07/../version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php];
    • [require_once] (not [require] as in course PHP 7) ensures that a file is not loaded twice, which would cause the fatal error “Cannot redeclare class … (previously declared in …)”;
  • lines 23–24: the full paths to the data files. Course PHP 7 stored them in constants created by the function [define]. Variables are sufficient;
  • line 31: the name of the file describing the database being used is displayed. In a string enclosed in quotation marks, the array element [$config["databaseFilename"]] must be enclosed in curly braces.

Results:

> php MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php
Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base décrite par [Data/database-pgsql.json]
Terminé

Similarly, the tax calculation script becomes the following [Main/MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php]:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the root directory for version 7: paths in the configuration file are relative to this directory
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// configuration file path
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json";

// retrieve the configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// Include the dependencies required by the script
foreach ($config["dependencies4calculate"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["dependencies"][$dependency];
}

// Data file paths
$databaseFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"];
$taxPayersDataFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["taxPayersDataFilename"];
$resultsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["resultsFilename"];
$errorsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["errorsFilename"];

try {
     // creating the layer [dao]
    $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase($databaseFilename);
     // Create the layer [métier]
    $métier = new Metier($dao);
     // Batch tax calculation
    $métier->executeBatchImpots($taxPayersDataFilename, $resultsFilename, $errorsFilename);
    print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [{$config["resultsFilename"]}]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // display error
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";
  • Lines 18–20: This time, the dependencies for the tax calculation are included;
  • lines 23–26: the file paths for the application’s JSON files;
  • lines 28–39: the rest of the code is the same as in version 6.

Results:

> php MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [Data/results.json]
Terminé

The generated [Data/results.json] file is identical to the [resultats.json] file from versions 5 and 6.

The names of the two scripts have changed. In course PHP 7, they referred to PostgreSQL ([MainTransferAdminDataFromFile2PostgresSQLDatabase.php], [MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInPostgresDatabase.php]). However, these scripts no longer depend on any specific SGBD: that value is selected by the [databaseFilename] key in the configuration file. If you replace ["Data/database-pgsql.json"] with ["Data/database-mysql.json"] in that file, the transfer script will use the MySQL database without changing a single line of PHP code:

> php MainTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database.php
Les données de l'administration fiscale ont été transférées dans la base décrite par [Data/database-mysql.json]
Terminé

This is the benefit of a configuration file: you can adapt the application to its environment (SGBD, file locations, etc.) without touching the code. We’ll see this configuration file again in future versions of the application.

docs.title: 15.2. Tests [PHPUnit]
docs.text: This version, like the previous ones, is validated by [PHPUnit] tests. Their environment is also built based on the configuration file.

docs.title: 15.2.1. [dao] Layer Test
docs.text:
The [dao] layer tests will use the two database descriptions from the [Data] folder: We will thus use the same tests to verify that the [dao] layer works with both MySQL and PostgreSQL. The [Tests/DaoTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// Test namespace
namespace Application\Tests;

// the classes being tested
use Application\DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase;
use Application\DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database;
use Application\TaxAdminData;
// the classes in PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class DaoTest extends TestCase
{
     // the root directory for version 7
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
     // the application configuration
    private static array $config;

     // run once, before the first class test
     #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
         // retrieve the configuration
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
         // Include the dependencies for tax calculation and data transfer
        $dependencies = array_unique([...self::$config["dependencies4calculate"], ...self::$config["dependencies4transfer"]]);
        foreach ($dependencies as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["dependencies"][$dependency];
        }
    }

     // the two databases
    public static function bases(): array
    {
         // [fichier de description de la base]
        return [
            "MySQL" => ["Data/database-mysql.json"],
            "PostgreSQL" => ["Data/database-pgsql.json"],
        ];
    }

     // tax administration data retrieved from the database
     #[DataProvider("bases")]
    public function testTaxAdminData(string $databaseFilename): void
    {
        $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$databaseFilename");
        $taxAdminData = $dao->getTaxAdminData();
         // calculation constants
        $this->assertSame(1551.0, $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(21037.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(42074.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCouplePourReduction);
        $this->assertSame(3797.0, $taxAdminData->valeurReducDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(1196.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCelibataire);
        $this->assertSame(1970.0, $taxAdminData->plafondDecoteCouple);
        $this->assertSame(1595.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCelibatairePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(2627.0, $taxAdminData->plafondImpotCouplePourDecote);
        $this->assertSame(12502.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMax);
        $this->assertSame(437.0, $taxAdminData->abattementDixPourcentMin);
         // tax brackets
        $this->assertSame([9964.0, 27519.0, 73779.0, 156244.0, 0.0], $taxAdminData->limites);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 0.14, 0.30, 0.41, 0.45], $taxAdminData->coeffR);
        $this->assertSame([0.0, 1394.96, 5798.0, 13913.69, 20163.45], $taxAdminData->coeffN);
    }

     // Transferring the file JSON to the database, then re-reading the database
     #[DataProvider("bases")]
    public function testTransfert(string $databaseFilename): void
    {
         // the JSON files
        $databaseFilename = self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$databaseFilename";
        $taxAdminDataFilename = self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["taxAdminDataFilename"];
         // transfer
        (new DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database($databaseFilename, $taxAdminDataFilename))->transferAdminData2Database();
         // database review by a layer [dao]
        $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase($databaseFilename);
         // the database contains the data from the file JSON
        $this->assertEquals(TaxAdminData::fromJsonFile($taxAdminDataFilename), $dao->getTaxAdminData());
    }
}

Comments

  • Lines 10–12: The tested classes are imported. The [use] statement does not load the classes; it merely allows them to be referred to by their short names;
  • line 22: the application configuration is stored in a static (class) attribute;
  • Lines 26–35: The static method [setUpBeforeClass] of [TestCase] is executed once, before the first test of the class. It reads the configuration file and loads the application files. Course PHP 7 performed this task at the top level of the test file, outside the class. With PHPUnit, this code is executed when PHPUnit loads the file, at a time that is not under our control; the [setUpBeforeClass] method is designed for this purpose;
  • Line 31: The tests for the [dao] layer require dependencies from the tax calculation (for class [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase]) and from the transfer (for class [DaoTransferAdminDataFromJsonFile2Database]). The two lists are combined, and then function [array_unique] removes the duplicates;
  • lines 38–45: the data source: the description files for the two databases;
  • lines 48–49: the [testTaxAdminData] test for version 5 is run once for each of the two databases;
  • lines 71–83: the same applies to the test for transferring data from the JSON file to the database.

docs.title: 15.2.2. Test of the [métier] layer
docs.text:
The [Tests/MetierTest.php] test is the Version 5 test with an environment built from the configuration file:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// Test namespace
namespace Application\Tests;

// the classes being tested
use Application\DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase;
use Application\InterfaceMetier;
use Application\Metier;
// the classes in PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class MetierTest extends TestCase
{
     // the root directory for version 7
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
     // the application configuration
    private static array $config;
     // the [métier] layer tested
    private InterfaceMetier $métier;

     // run once, before the first class test
     #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
         // retrieve the configuration
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
         // Include the dependencies for the tax calculation
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies4calculate"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["dependencies"][$dependency];
        }
    }

     // executed before each test
     #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
         // creates the layer [dao] based on the configuration database
        $dao = new DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["databaseFilename"]);
         // creation of the layer [métier]
        $this->métier = new Metier($dao);
    }

Comments

  • Lines 28–36: The configuration file is read, and the dependencies for the tax calculation are loaded, just as the main script [MainCalculateImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] does;
  • Line 43: The layer [dao] uses the database specified by the configuration file;
  • The data provider [contribuables] and the method [testCalculerImpot], not shown here, are those from version 4.

We have now completed the console versions of the tax calculation application. Version 8 will transform it into a client/server application: the database and the tax calculation will reside on a web server, queried by clients. It will incorporate the classes from version 5 and the configuration file technique from version 7.

docs.title: 18. Practical Exercise – Version 8
docs.text: We’ll revisit the sample application—version 5 (and its version 7 configured by the file JSON)—and turn it into a client/server application. This will allow us to put into practice what we learned in the previous chapter about web services.

docs.title: 18.1. Introduction
docs.text:
The architecture of version 5 was as follows:

  • the layer named [dao] (Data Access Objects) handles interactions with the database MySQL and the local file system;
  • the layer named [métier] performs the tax calculation;
  • The main script acts as the orchestrator: it instantiates the layers [dao] and [métier], then communicates with the layer [métier] to perform the necessary tasks.

We are going to migrate this architecture to the following client/server architecture:

  • In [2], we will reuse the [dao] layer from version 5, removing the methods that access the local file system. These methods will be migrated to the [dao] layer of the [6, 7] client;
  • in [3], the [métier] layer will remain the same as in version 5, minus its [executeBatchImpots] method, which is migrated to the [métier] and [8] layers of the client;
  • In [4], the server script must be written; it will need to:
    • create the layers [métier], [dao], and [3, 2];
    • communicate with the client script [5, 7];
  • In [7], the client layer [dao] must be written:
    • it will be a client HTTP of the server script [4, 5];
    • It will adopt the methods for accessing the local file system from the [dao] layer of Version 5;
  • In [8], the client’s [métier] layer will provide the same methods as the [InterfaceMetier] interface from Version 5. However, its implementation will be different. In version 5, the [métier] layer performed the tax calculation. Here, the server’s [métier] layer performs this calculation. The client-side layer [métier] will therefore call upon the layers [dao] and [7] to communicate with the server and request that it calculate the tax;
  • In [9], the console script will need to instantiate the client layers [dao, métier] and launch their execution.

The server is a web script: it is located in the [scripts-web/impots/version-08] folder and executed by the Apache server in [Laragon]. The client is a console script: it is located in the [scripts-console/impots/version-08] folder and executed in a terminal.

docs.title: 18.2. The Server
docs.text:
We are focusing on the server-side of the application.

This architecture will be implemented by the following files:

scripts-web/impots/version-08
├── Dao
│   ├── InterfaceServerDao.php
│   └── ServerDao.php
├── Data
│   ├── .htaccess
│   ├── config-server.json
│   ├── database-mysql.json
│   └── database-pgsql.json
├── Metier
│   ├── InterfaceServerMetier.php
│   └── ServerMetier.php
├── Tests
│   ├── ServerDaoTest.php
│   └── ServerMetierTest.php
└── impots-server.php

docs.title: 18.2.1. Entities Exchanged Between Layers
docs.text: The entities exchanged between the layers are those from version 5: the [ExceptionImpots] exception, the tax administration data [TaxAdminData], and the database description [Database]. The server also uses the Version 5 class [Utilitaires], whose method [lireFichierJson] is used by the class [Database]. Course PHP 7 used to copy these files to the server folder. We now load them directly from the [scripts-console/impots/version-05] folder: this ensures that each class exists as a single instance, and any correction made in version 5 benefits all versions that use it.

docs.title: 18.2.2. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [dao] layer implements the following [InterfaceServerDao] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the server’s [dao] layer interface
interface InterfaceServerDao
{
     // Reading data from the tax authority
     // throws a [ExceptionImpots] exception in case of an error
    public function getTaxAdminData(): TaxAdminData;
}
  • Line 13: The [getTaxAdminData] method retrieves data from the tax authority’s database.

The [InterfaceServerDao] interface is implemented by the following [ServerDao] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the server's [dao] layer: it retrieves tax authority data from a database
// this is the [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class from version 5 without the methods
// that work with taxpayers' JSON files
class ServerDao implements InterfaceServerDao
{
     // the database description
    private readonly Database $database;
     // the object of type [TaxAdminData] containing data from the tax authority
     // [protected]: derived classes can initialize it
    protected readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

     // the constructor
    public function __construct(string $databaseFilename)
    {
         // the database description—may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots]
        $this->database = Database::fromJsonFile($databaseFilename);
        $database = $this->database;
        try {
             // opens the connection to the database
             // the read rows will be returned as associative arrays [colonne => valeur]
            $connexion = \PDO::connect(
                $database->dsn,
                $database->id,
                $database->pwd,
                [\PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => \PDO::FETCH_ASSOC]
            );
             // Start a transaction
            $connexion->beginTransaction();
             // Read the tax bracket table
            $tranches = $this->getTranches($connexion);
             // read the constants table
            $constantes = $this->getConstantes($connexion);
             // the transaction is successfully completed
            $connexion->commit();
        } catch (\PDOException $ex) {
             // Is there a transaction in progress?
            if (isset($connexion) && $connexion->inTransaction()) {
                 // End the transaction upon failure
                $connexion->rollBack();
            }
             // The error is propagated to the calling code as an exception [ExceptionImpots]
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur d'accès à la base de données ({$ex->getMessage()})", 30, $ex);
        }
         // constructing the object [TaxAdminData]: the read data is verified
        $this->taxAdminData = TaxAdminData::fromArray([...$tranches, ...$constantes]);
    }

This is the code for the [DaoImpotsWithTaxAdminDataInDatabase] class from version 5, presented in Chapter 13, without the [TraitDao] feature that provided the methods for reading and writing taxpayers’ JSON files. The private methods [getTranches] and [getConstantes] that follow—not reproduced here—remain unchanged. There is only one difference:

  • line 17: the attribute [taxAdminData] is declared as [protected] instead of [private]. Version 9 will derive the [ServerDao] class, and the derived class must be able to initialize this attribute. Starting with PHP 8.4, a derived class can initialize an inherited [readonly] attribute, provided that it is not private.

docs.title: 18.2.3. The [métier] layer
docs.text:
The [métier] layer implements the following [InterfaceServerMetier] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the server's [métier] layer interface
interface InterfaceServerMetier
{
     // calculation of a taxpayer’s tax
     // returns the table [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;
}

The [InterfaceServerMetier] interface is implemented by the following [ServerMetier] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the server layer [métier]: the [Metier] class from version 5 without the [executeBatchImpots] method
class ServerMetier implements InterfaceServerMetier
{
     // tax administration data
    private readonly TaxAdminData $taxAdminData;

     // the [dao] layer is injected by the constructor
    public function __construct(private readonly InterfaceServerDao $dao)
    {
         // Data required to calculate the tax is retrieved
         // The method [getTaxAdminData] may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots]
         // it is then allowed to propagate back to the calling code
        $this->taxAdminData = $this->dao->getTaxAdminData();
    }

     // Tax Calculation
    // --------------------------------------------------------------------------
     #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
  • Line 9: The class [ServerMetier] is the class [Metier] from version 5 without its method [executeBatchImpots];
  • line 15: The constructor receives a reference to a [dao] layer of type [InterfaceServerDao];
  • line 26: the [calculerImpot] method and the private methods it uses remain unchanged. The algorithm was discussed and explained starting in Version 1, and its object-oriented version is covered in Chapter 13.

docs.title: 18.2.4. The server script
docs.text:
The server script [impots-server.php] implements the [web] and [4] layers. It is configured by the following JSON and [Data/config-server.json] files:

{
    "databaseFilename": "Data/database-mysql.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/TaxAdminData.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Entities/Database.php",
        "../../../scripts-console/impots/version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "Dao/InterfaceServerDao.php",
        "Dao/ServerDao.php",
        "Metier/InterfaceServerMetier.php",
        "Metier/ServerMetier.php"
    ],
    "users": [
        {
            "login": "admin",
            "passwd": "admin"
        }
    ]
}
  • Line 2: the JSON configuration file for the MySQL database. This is the [database-mysql.json] file from version 7. The [Data] folder also contains the [database-pgsql.json] file for the PostgreSQL database: simply change this line so that the server works with PostgreSQL;
  • Lines 3–12: the PHP files for the application, whose paths are relative to the [version-08] folder on the server. The first four are from version 5;
  • lines 13–18: the list of users authorized to use the application.

As in version 7, the [rootDirectory] key no longer exists: the script calculates its own root folder based on the constant [__DIR__]. There is also no longer a [absoluteDependencies] key, which provided the absolute path to the [vendor/autoload.php] file from [Composer]: it is now determined based on [__DIR__].

The file [config-server.json] is located in the [Data] folder on the server, and thus within the website’s directory structure: without taking precautions, anyone could download it along with URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/Data/config-server.json] and read the user credentials. The same applies to the file [database-mysql.json], which contains the database password. The [Data] folder therefore contains a file named [.htaccess]:

# The directory [Data] contains passwords: Apache refuses to serve its files
Require all denied

A file named [.htaccess] contains Apache server configuration directives that apply to the folder containing it and its subfolders. The [Require all denied] directive denies access to the folder: Apache responds with [403 Forbidden] to any request for a file in the [Data] folder. The PHP script, on the other hand, reads these files from the disk without going through Apache and is not affected.

The script [impots-server.php] implements the [web] layer as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\JsonResponse;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

// the server's root directory: paths in the configuration file are relative to this directory
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__;
// Configuration file path
const CONFIG_FILENAME = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-server.json";

// retrieve the configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(CONFIG_FILENAME), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// Include the dependencies required by the script
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// Preparing the server's response JSON
$response = new JsonResponse();
// accented characters and unescaped characters; real numbers are always written with a decimal point (0.0)
$response->setEncodingOptions(JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION);

// Retrieve the current request
$request = Request::createFromGlobals();
// Authentication: credentials sent by the client (null if none were sent)
$requestUser = $request->getUser();
$requestPassword = $request->getPassword();
// Is the user one of the authorized users?
$trouvé = $requestUser !== null && $requestPassword !== null
    && array_any(
        $config["users"],
        fn(array $user): bool => $user["login"] === $requestUser && hash_equals($user["passwd"], $requestPassword)
    );
if (!$trouvé) {
     // Not found—code 401
    $response->setStatusCode(Response::HTTP_UNAUTHORIZED);
    $response->headers->set("WWW-Authenticate", 'Basic realm="Serveur de calcul des impots"');
     // error message
    $response->setData(["réponse" => ["erreur" => "Echec de l'authentification [$requestUser]"]]);
    $response->send();
     // end
    exit;
}

// A valid user was found—checking the received parameters
$erreurs = [];
// A request with three parameters is required: GET
if ($request->getMethod() !== "GET" || $request->query->count() !== 3) {
    $erreurs[] = "Méthode GET requise avec les seuls paramètres [marié, enfants, salaire]";
}
// marital status
if (!$request->query->has("marié")) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié manquant";
} else {
    $marié = strtolower(trim($request->query->getString("marié")));
    if (!in_array($marié, ["oui", "non"], true)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre marié [$marié] invalide";
    }
}
// number of children and salary: integers >= 0
$valeurs = [];
foreach (["enfants", "salaire"] as $paramètre) {
    if (!$request->query->has($paramètre)) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre manquant";
        continue;
    }
    $valeur = trim($request->query->getString($paramètre));
    if (preg_match('/^\d+$/', $valeur) !== 1) {
        $erreurs[] = "paramètre $paramètre [$valeur] invalide";
    } else {
        $valeurs[$paramètre] = (int) $valeur;
    }
}
// Any other parameters in the query?
foreach (array_diff(array_keys($request->query->all()), ["marié", "enfants", "salaire"]) as $paramètre) {
    $erreurs[] = "paramètre [$paramètre] invalide";
}
// Errors?
if ($erreurs !== []) {
     // A 400 error code is sent to the client
    $response->setStatusCode(Response::HTTP_BAD_REQUEST);
    $response->setData(["réponse" => ["erreurs" => $erreurs]]);
    $response->send();
    exit;
}

// We have everything we need to proceed
// creating the server architecture
try {
     // Creating the layer [dao]
    $dao = new ServerDao(ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["databaseFilename"]);
     // Creating the layer [métier]
    $métier = new ServerMetier($dao);
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // An error message from a SGBD driver may not be encoded in UTF-8 (Windows-1252 on Windows)
    $message = $ex->getMessage();
    if (!mb_check_encoding($message, "UTF-8")) {
        $message = mb_convert_encoding($message, "UTF-8", "Windows-1252");
    }
     // An error code 500 is sent to the client
    $response->setStatusCode(Response::HTTP_INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR);
    $response->setData(["réponse" => ["erreur" => $message]]);
    $response->send();
    exit;
}
// Tax calculation
$result = $métier->calculerImpot($marié, $valeurs["enfants"], $valeurs["salaire"]);
// the response is returned
$response->setData(["réponse" => $result]);
$response->send();

Comments

  • lines 10–12: the classes from the [HttpFoundation] library that will be used are declared;
  • Line 15: The server’s root directory is the script’s directory;
  • line 20: the configuration file is loaded;
  • Lines 23–26: We load the class loader from [Composer], then all the application files;
  • line 29: we prepare a JSON response. The [JsonResponse] class is a subclass of [Response]: its [setData] method encodes the array passed to it into JSON and uses it as the response body. It also sets the header HTTP [Content-Type: application/json];
  • Line 31: The options for function [json_encode], which is used by [setData]. With [JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE], accented characters are not encoded in [\uXXXX]. With [JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION], the actual tax rate [0.0] is written as [0.0] and not [0]: the client will decode it as a floating-point number (float) and not as an integer;
  • lines 36–37: We retrieve the identifiers sent by the client, as in the previous chapter;
  • lines 39–43: We verify that the user is indeed one of the authorized users. The function [array_any] (PHP 8.4) returns [true] if at least one element of the array [$config["users"]] satisfies the condition expressed by the arrow function passed to it. It replaces the [while] loop in the PHP script. 7. Passwords are compared using [hash_equals];
  • lines 44–52: if this is not the case, the code HTTP [401 Unauthorized] is sent, indicating that access has been denied. Upon receiving this code and the header HTTP [WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm=…], browsers display an authentication window prompting the user to authenticate;
  • Line 49: The server’s response, JSON, explains the cause of the error. All server responses will be the string JSON from an array [["réponse" => qqChose]]. The script PHP 7 returned the rejected username and password to the client. A password must never be returned or written to logs: we only return the username;
  • Lines 56–88: We verify the validity of the request:
    • a GET request with exactly three parameters;
    • a parameter [marié] whose value must be [oui] or [non];
    • a parameter [enfants], whose value must be an integer >= 0;
    • a parameter [salaire], whose value must be an integer greater than or equal to 0;
    • no other parameters;
  • line 59: each time an error is detected, an error message is added to the array [$erreurs];
  • line 65: the method [getString] of the object [$request->query] returns the parameter value as a character string;
  • line 72: The parameters [enfants] and [salaire] follow the same rule: they are checked in the same loop. Their values, converted to integers, are placed in the array [$valeurs];
  • line 85: The function [array_diff] returns the names of the received parameters that are not in the list [marié, enfants, salaire];
  • line 89: if an error occurs, the code HTTP [400 Bad Request] is sent to the client. The response JSON contains the list of errors;
  • Lines 99–104: From this point on, the query has been validated. The [dao, métier] layers can be instantiated. This instantiation incurs a cost (reading the database) and should only be performed if you are certain the query is valid. Constructing the [dao] layer may throw a [ExceptionImpots]-type exception;
  • lines 106–108: The error message is often that of the PDO driver for SGBD. On Windows, it may sometimes be encoded in Windows-1252 rather than UTF-8. However, the [json_encode] function only accepts UTF-8 strings: [JsonResponse] would then throw an exception. The [mb_check_encoding] function checks the string’s encoding, and the [mb_convert_encoding] function converts it if necessary. The script PHP 7 used the function [utf8_encode], which has been deprecated since PHP 8.2;
  • line 111: if an exception occurred, then the code HTTP [500 Internal Server Error] is sent to the client. This code indicates that the server was unable to process a valid request. The response explains the cause of the error;
  • line 117: the tax calculation is delegated to the [métier] layer;
  • Lines 119–120: Send the response, with the default status code [200 OK].

Let’s test this script. In a browser, request URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?marié=oui&enfants=2&salaire=55555]. The browser displays its authentication window, where you enter [admin] and [admin]. It then displays the server’s response: JSON. If the server rejects these credentials, see the section “When the server always responds with 401” in the previous chapter.

docs.title: 18.2.4.1. Why [http] and not [https]?
docs.text:
The client sends its credentials: strictly speaking, the URL should be secured ([https]), as we saw in the previous chapter. But modern browsers ([Chrome], [Edge], [Firefox]) will only accept a HTTPS page if the server certificate is issued by a certificate authority they trust. The certificate that [Laragon] generates for [localhost] is self-signed: it is not guaranteed by anyone. Depending on the browser version and the state of its cache, the browser either displays a warning with a link ([Continuer vers localhost (dangereux)]) or refuses to load the page without offering the option to proceed. This happens when the browser has recorded that [localhost] must always be served with a valid certificate (HSTS mechanism), or when it deems the certificate non-compliant. The solutions described in the previous chapter (adding the [Laragon] certificate to the [Windows] certificate store, deleting the HSTS rule) are not always sufficient.

We therefore use the unsecured URL certificate in the browser instead of [http://localhost/...]. This is not a security lapse here: a request to [localhost] never leaves the machine (it passes through the internal network interface, known as the “loopback” interface), and no spyware can intercept it on the network. Web browsers are aware of this, by the way: they treat [http://localhost] as a trusted origin. On the other hand, as soon as the server is accessible from the network—and especially in a production environment—the HTTPS protocol is essential, along with a valid certificate issued by a recognized authority (for example, free of charge, by [Let's Encrypt]).

The clients we write, however, are not browsers: the [curl] command (option [-k]) and the Symfony client [HttpClient] (options [verify_peer] through [false]) can accept the self-signed certificate from [Laragon]. However, this requires that the HTTPS protocol have been enabled in [Laragon] ([Apache / SSL / Enabled] menu), which is not the case by default, and that this certificate be usable on the machine. To ensure the examples work on any [Laragon] installation, we will therefore use URL and [http://localhost/...] throughout this chapter and the following ones: in the browser, in the [curl] commands, and in the client configuration files ([urlServer] key). To switch to HTTPS, simply replace [http] with [https] in these URL and add the [-k] option to the [curl] commands: The client configuration files already contain the necessary options [verify_peer] and [verify_host], which have no effect when used with [http]. The results are the same with both schemes.

Let’s run the same query with [curl]. The non-ASCII characters in a URL must be encoded: the character [é] in the parameter [marié] is encoded as [%C3%A9] (its two bytes as UTF-8). A browser performs this encoding itself:

> curl -i -u admin:admin "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=oui&enfants=2&salaire=55555"
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 12:29:49 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json

{"réponse":{"impôt":2814,"surcôte":0,"décôte":0,"réduction":0,"taux":0.14}}
  • line 2: the code [200 OK];
  • line 8: the header HTTP [Content-Type: application/json] defined by the class [JsonResponse];
  • Line 10: The server's response JSON.

Without credentials (no [-u] option), the code [401 Unauthorized] is returned:

> curl -i "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=oui&enfants=2&salaire=55555"
HTTP/1.0 401 Unauthorized
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 12:29:49 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="Serveur de calcul des impots"
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json

{"réponse":{"erreur":"Echec de l'authentification []"}}

Let’s run a few error tests. We request URL and [http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?marié=x&enfants=x&salaire=x&w=x]:

> curl -i -u admin:admin "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=x&enfants=x&salaire=x&w=x"
HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 12:29:49 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close
Content-Type: application/json

{"réponse":{"erreurs":["Méthode GET requise avec les seuls paramètres [marié, enfants, salaire]","paramètre marié [x] invalide","paramètre enfants [x] invalide","paramètre salaire [x] invalide","paramètre [w] invalide"]}}

A POST request without parameters (option [-X POST] from [curl]):

> curl -i -u admin:admin -X POST "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php"
HTTP/1.0 400 Bad Request

Now let’s simulate a failure of SGBD. We can stop MySQL from the [Laragon] window. Instead, we changed the DSN entry in the [database-mysql.json] file to [mysql:host=127.0.0.1;port=3307;dbname=dbimpots-2019;charset=utf8mb4]: no SGBD is listening on port 3307, and the connection is refused, just as it would be if MySQL were stopped:

> curl -i -u admin:admin "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=oui&enfants=3&salaire=60000"
HTTP/1.0 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 12:29:50 GMT
Server: Apache/2.4.58 (Ubuntu)
X-Powered-By: PHP/8.5.11
Cache-Control: no-cache, private
Connection: close

{"réponse":{"erreur":"Erreur d'accès à la base de données (SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused)"}}
  • line 2: the code [500 Internal Server Error];
  • line 10: the exception message [ExceptionImpots] thrown by the [dao] layer. On Windows, the driver message is in French: [Aucune connexion n'a pu être établie car l'ordinateur cible l'a expressément refusée].

Then restore the original DSN.

docs.title: 18.2.5. [PHPUnit] Tests
docs.text: Each time we build a new version of the server, we will test the layers [dao] and [métier], as has been done since version 4. These tests do not go through the web server: they build the [dao] and [métier] layers just as the server script does and test them directly. They are located in the [Tests] folder on the server. Course PHP 7 used the [Codeception] testing framework; we are using [PHPUnit], as in the previous chapters.

docs.title: 18.2.5.1. [dao] Layer Tests
docs.text:
The [Tests/ServerDaoTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// Test namespace
namespace Application\Tests;

// The class under test
use Application\ServerDao;
// the classes in PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

final class ServerDaoTest extends TestCase
{
     // the server's root directory
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
     // server configuration
    private static array $config;

     // executed once, before the first test of the class
     #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
         // retrieve the server configuration
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-server.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
         // Include the server dependencies
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
        }
    }

     // Tax administration data read from the database
    public function testTaxAdminData(): void
    {
         // creating the layer [dao] as in the server script
        $dao = new ServerDao(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . self::$config["databaseFilename"]);
        $taxAdminData = $dao->getTaxAdminData();
         // calculation constants
        $this->assertSame(1551.0, $taxAdminData->plafondQfDemiPart);
        $this->assertSame(21037.0, $taxAdminData->plafondRevenusCelibatairePourReduction);

Comments

  • Lines 23–31: We set up the same working environment as in the server script [impots-server.php]: reading the configuration file and loading the application files. The class loader for [Composer] does not need to be loaded: [PHPUnit] has already done so;
  • Line 37: We create an instance of the [dao] layer to be tested, just as is done in the server script;
  • From this point on, the conditions are the same as in the server script: the remainder of the [testTaxAdminData] method, not reproduced here, is the same as the [DaoTest] test for versions 5 through 7.

docs.title: 18.2.5.2. Tests for layer [métier]
docs.text:

     // run once, before the first test in the class

    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void

docs.title: 18.3.1. Entities Exchanged Between Layers
docs.text:
The client entities have all been described and are already used in version 5:

  • the exception [ExceptionImpots];
  • the data for taxpayer [TaxPayerData].

Like the server, the client loads them from the Version 5 folder, along with the class [Utilitaires] and the trait [TraitDao].

docs.title: 18.3.2. The [dao] layer
docs.text:
The [dao] layer implements the following [InterfaceClientDao] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the client interface for layer [dao]
// All methods throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception in case of an error
interface InterfaceClientDao
{
     // Reading taxpayer data
     // Invalid data is flagged in the file JSON [$errorsFilename]
     /** @return TaxPayerData[] */
    public function getTaxPayersData(string $taxPayersFilename, string $errorsFilename): array;

     // Calculation of a taxpayer's tax by the server
     // returns the table [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

     // Saves the results
     /** @param TaxPayerData[] $taxPayersData */
    public function saveResults(string $resultsFilename, array $taxPayersData): void;
}
  • Line 15: The [getTaxPayersData] method loads taxpayer data from the JSON and [$taxPayersFilename] files into memory. If there are any errors, they are logged in the JSON and [$errorsFilename] files;
  • line 19: the [calculerImpot] method calculates a taxpayer’s tax;
  • line 23: the method [saveResults] saves the data from table [$taxPayersData]—which represents the results of several tax calculations—to file [$resultsFilename].

The methods [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] are part of the [InterfaceDao] interface in version 5. The [InterfaceClientDao] interface is implemented by the following [ClientDao] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// Symfony dependencies
use Symfony\Component\HttpClient\HttpClient;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\Exception\ExceptionInterface;
use Symfony\Contracts\HttpClient\HttpClientInterface;

// the client layer [dao]: a client of the tax calculation server HTTP
class ClientDao implements InterfaceClientDao
{
     // The version 5 feature implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods of the interface
    use TraitDao;

     // the HTTP client
    private readonly HttpClientInterface $httpClient;

     // manufacturer
     // $urlServer: the URL of the tax calculation server
     // $user: the user making the requests, table [login, passwd]
     // $httpClientOptions: additional client options: HTTP (verify_peer, verify_host...)
    public function __construct(
        private readonly string $urlServer,
         #[\SensitiveParameter] array $user,
        array $httpClientOptions = [],
    ) {
         // the client HTTP: the user's credentials will be sent with each request
        $this->httpClient = HttpClient::create([
            ...$httpClientOptions,
            "auth_basic" => [$user["login"], $user["passwd"]],
        ]);
    }

     // tax calculation by the server
     #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        try {
             // The request is sent to the server
            $response = $this->httpClient->request("GET", $this->urlServer, [
                "query" => [
                    "marié" => $marié,
                    "enfants" => $enfants,
                    "salaire" => $salaire,
                ],
            ]);
             // response status
            $statusCode = $response->getStatusCode();
             // the response document JSON, even if the status is an error code (false parameter)
            $json = $response->getContent(false);
        } catch (ExceptionInterface $ex) {
             // The server could not be reached
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Erreur de communication avec le serveur ({$ex->getMessage()})", 40, $ex);
        }
         // logs
         // print "$json\n";
         // the server sends the string JSON from an array ["réponse" => qqChose]
        try {
            $réponse = json_decode($json, true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)["réponse"] ?? null;
        } catch (\JsonException $ex) {
            $réponse = null;
        }
        if (!is_array($réponse)) {
            throw new ExceptionImpots("Réponse du serveur invalide [$json]", 41);
        }
         // error?
        if ($statusCode !== 200) {
             // an exception is thrown with a message consisting of the server's response supplemented by its status: HTTP
            $message = json_encode(
                ["statut HTTP" => $statusCode] + $réponse,
                JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR
            );
            throw new ExceptionImpots($message, 42);
        }
         // the response is returned: the array [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
        return $réponse;
    }
}

Comments

  • line 17: We insert the [TraitDao] class from version 5, which implements the [getTaxPayersData] and [saveResults] methods. This leaves only the [calculerImpot] method to be implemented;
  • line 20: the client HTTP of [Symfony], of the type of the interface [HttpClientInterface];
  • lines 26–30: The constructor of the [ClientDao] class takes three parameters:
    • the URL [$urlServer] from the tax calculation server. This is a parameter promoted to an attribute (constructor property promotion);
    • the array [$user] of keys [login] and [passwd], which defines the user making the requests. The attribute [#[\SensitiveParameter]] (PHP 8.2) instructs PHP to hide the value of this parameter in the stack traces displayed in the event of an error: the password will not appear there;
    • additional options for the HTTP client;
  • lines 32–35: the client HTTP is created once and for all, with the received options, which are supplemented by the option [auth_basic]: the user’s credentials will be sent with each request. The operator [...] copies the elements from the array [$httpClientOptions] into the options array. The client PHP 7 created a new client HTTP for each request;
  • line 40: The [calculerImpot] method receives the three parameters to be sent to the tax calculation server;
  • lines 44–50: The server is queried with the three parameters it expects. The [query] option adds these parameters to URL after encoding them ([marié] becomes [mari%C3%A9]);
  • Line 54: The response JSON is retrieved from the server. If the parameter [false] is not passed to the method [getContent], then, if the server’s response status indicates an error (3xx–5xx codes), the HTTP client throws an exception as soon as an attempt is made to retrieve the response content. Here, regardless of the HTTP status of the response, we want to access its content, which explains the error;
  • Lines 55–57: If the server could not be reached, the HTTP client throws a [ExceptionInterface] exception. We convert it to a [ExceptionImpots] exception: this way, the client’s upper layers only have to handle one exception type;
  • line 60: In development mode, the server’s JSON response can be displayed;
  • Lines 63–68: The server's response is the string JSON from an array [["réponse" => qqChose]]. We retrieve the [qqChose]. If the received document is not JSON (for example, an Apache error page HTML), we throw a [ExceptionImpots] exception;
  • lines 71–77: if the status code HTTP is not 200, then the server has encountered a problem. An exception of type [ExceptionImpots] is then thrown, with a message consisting of the server’s response JSON appended with the response code HTTP. The operator [+] combines two associative arrays;
  • line 80: the result is returned as an associative array with keys [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux].

docs.title: 18.3.3. The [métier] layer
docs.text:
The [métier] [8] layer implements the following [InterfaceClientMetier] interface:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the client's [métier] layer interface
interface InterfaceClientMetier
{
     // Tax calculation for a taxpayer
     // returns the table [impôt, surcôte, décôte, réduction, taux]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array;

     // Tax calculation in batch mode
     // may throw an exception [ExceptionImpots] propagated from the [dao] layer
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void;
}
  • Line 13: The [calculerImpot] method calculates the tax;
  • line 17: the [executeBatchImpots] method calculates the tax for taxpayers whose data is in the [$taxPayersFileName] file, writes the results to the [$resultsFileName] file, and writes any errors encountered to the [$errorsFileName] file.

These are the two methods of the [InterfaceMetier] interface in version 5. The [InterfaceClientMetier] interface is implemented by the following [ClientMetier] class:

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the client’s [métier] layer: tax calculation is performed by the server
class ClientMetier implements InterfaceClientMetier
{
     // The [dao] layer is injected by the constructor
    public function __construct(private readonly InterfaceClientDao $clientDao)
    {
    }

     // Tax calculation: it is delegated to the [dao] layer, which queries the server
     #[\Override]
    public function calculerImpot(string $marié, int $enfants, int $salaire): array
    {
        return $this->clientDao->calculerImpot($marié, $enfants, $salaire);
    }

     // Tax calculation in batch mode
     #[\Override]
    public function executeBatchImpots(string $taxPayersFileName, string $resultsFileName, string $errorsFileName): void
    {
         // allow exceptions originating from the [dao] layer to be propagated
         // retrieve taxpayer data
        $taxPayersData = $this->clientDao->getTaxPayersData($taxPayersFileName, $errorsFileName);
         // Calculate the tax for each taxpayer
        $results = array_map(
            fn(TaxPayerData $taxPayerData): TaxPayerData => $taxPayerData->avecRésultats(
                $this->calculerImpot($taxPayerData->marié, $taxPayerData->enfants, $taxPayerData->salaire)
            ),
            $taxPayersData
        );
         // Save the results
        $this->clientDao->saveResults($resultsFileName, $results);
    }
}

Comments

  • line 12: The constructor of the [ClientMetier] class receives a reference to the [dao] layer as a parameter;
  • Lines 18–20: The tax calculation is delegated to the [dao] layer;
  • lines 25–38: The method [executeBatchImpots] is that of the [Metier] class in version 5.

docs.title: 18.3.4. The main script
docs.text:
The client script [Main/MainImpotsClient.php] implements the layers [console] and [9]. It is configured by the following file: JSON and [Data/config-client.json]:

{
    "urlServer": "http://localhost/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php",
    "user": {
        "login": "admin",
        "passwd": "admin"
    },
    "httpClientOptions": {
        "verify_peer": false,
        "verify_host": false
    },
    "taxPayersDataFilename": "Data/taxpayersdata.json",
    "resultsFilename": "Data/results.json",
    "errorsFilename": "Data/errors.json",
    "dependencies": [
        "../version-05/Entities/ExceptionImpots.php",
        "../version-05/Entities/TaxPayerData.php",
        "../version-05/Utilities/Utilitaires.php",
        "../version-05/Dao/TraitDao.php",
        "Dao/InterfaceClientDao.php",
        "Dao/ClientDao.php",
        "Metier/InterfaceClientMetier.php",
        "Metier/ClientMetier.php"
    ]
}
  • Line 2: the URL from the tax calculation server. It uses the [http] schema: we saw why earlier;
  • Lines 3–6: the user sending requests to the tax calculation server;
  • lines 7–9: the HTTP client options. They are only used with a URL or [https]: as in the previous chapter, they instruct the client not to verify the server’s self-signed certificate. When used with a URL or [http], these options are ignored;
  • lines 11–13: the JSON files containing taxpayer data, results, and errors;
  • lines 14–23: the various PHP files from the client. The first four are those for version 5.

The code for the [MainImpotsClient.php] script is as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function results
declare(strict_types=1);

// namespace
namespace Application;

// the client’s root directory: paths to the configuration file are relative to this directory
const ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
// the configuration file in the [Data] folder: first command-line argument if it exists
$configFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/" . ($argv[1] ?? "config-client.json");

// retrieve the configuration
$config = json_decode(file_get_contents($configFilename), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);

// Include the dependencies required by the script: third-party libraries (Symfony), followed by application files
require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/../../../vendor/autoload.php";
foreach ($config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
    require_once ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
}

// paths to the data files
$taxPayersDataFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["taxPayersDataFilename"];
$resultsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["resultsFilename"];
$errorsFilename = ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/" . $config["errorsFilename"];

// creation of the [dao] layer
$clientDao = new ClientDao($config["urlServer"], $config["user"], $config["httpClientOptions"]);
// Creating the layer [métier]
$clientMetier = new ClientMetier($clientDao);

// Batch tax calculation
try {
    $clientMetier->executeBatchImpots($taxPayersDataFilename, $resultsFilename, $errorsFilename);
    print "Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [{$config["resultsFilename"]}]\n";
} catch (ExceptionImpots $ex) {
     // display error
    print "Erreur n° {$ex->getCode()} : {$ex->getMessage()}\n";
}
// end
print "Terminé\n";

Comments

  • line 10: the client’s root folder is the parent folder of the [Main] folder;
  • line 12: the configuration file, located in the [Data] folder. Its name can be passed as an argument to the script ([php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-ko.json]). Otherwise, the default is the [config-client.json] file. We will use this option for error testing;
  • Lines 18–21: Loading dependencies: the [Composer] class loader for the Symfony [HttpClient] library, followed by the client files;
  • line 29: creating the [dao] layer. We pass the information the layer constructor expects to it:
    • the URL from the tax calculation server;
    • the credentials of the user who will make the requests;
    • the options for the HTTP client;
  • Line 31: Creation of the [métier] layer. A reference to the [dao] layer that was just created is passed to the layer constructor;
  • line 35: the [métier] layer is instructed to:
    • calculate the taxes for all taxpayers in the [taxpayersdata.json] file;
    • write the results to the file [results.json];
    • write the errors to the file [errors.json];
  • Lines 37–39: All client errors, including communication errors with the server, occur as a [ExceptionImpots] exception, for which the code and message are displayed.

With the Apache server and SGBD MySQL running, let’s run the client in a terminal opened in the [Main] folder:

> php MainImpotsClient.php
Les résultats ont été enregistrés dans le fichier [Data/results.json]
Terminé

Running the client produces the same results as in previous versions. Check the following files:

  • [Data/taxpayersdata.json]: data for taxpayers for whom the tax amount is calculated;
  • [Data/results.json]: results for the various taxpayers in the [Data/taxpayersdata.json] file. This file is identical to the [results.json] file from version 7;
  • [Data/errors.json]: errors that may have occurred while processing the [Data/taxpayersdata.json] file.

Let’s look at the possible error scenarios. First, an unreachable server. You can stop the Apache server for [Laragon]. Instead, we used the configuration file [config-client-injoignable.json], which is identical to the file [config-client.json] except for URL: this one specifies port 4443 on the [localhost] machine, on which no server is listening for requests ([http://localhost:4443/php8-oct-2026/...]). The results in the client console are then as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-injoignable.json
Erreur n° 40 : Erreur de communication avec le serveur (Failed to connect to localhost port 4443 after 0 ms: Couldn't connect to server for "http://localhost:4443/php8-oct-2026/scripts-web/impots/version-08/impots-server.php?mari%C3%A9=oui&enfants=2&salaire=55555".)
Terminé

The exception thrown by the Symfony client HTTP was converted by the [dao] layer into a [ExceptionImpots] exception with code 40.

Now, let’s simulate a failure of SGBD MySQL, in the same way as we did previously with [curl]. The results in the client console are as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php
Erreur n° 42 : {"statut HTTP":500,"erreur":"Erreur d'accès à la base de données (SQLSTATE[HY000] [2002] Connection refused)"}
Terminé

Let’s restore the SGBD, then use the configuration file [config-client-ko.json], in which the logging-in user is unknown to the server:

    "user": {
        "login": "x",
        "passwd": "x"
    },

The results in the client console are then as follows:

> php MainImpotsClient.php config-client-ko.json
Erreur n° 42 : {"statut HTTP":401,"erreur":"Echec de l'authentification [x]"}
Terminé

docs.title: 18.3.5. [PHPUnit] Tests
docs.text:
As we did for previous versions, we will write a test named [PHPUnit] for the client’s [métier] layer. The [Tests/ClientMetierTest.php] test is as follows:

<?php

// Strict adherence to the declared types of parameters and function return values
declare(strict_types=1);

// Test namespace
namespace Application\Tests;

// the classes being tested
use Application\ClientDao;
use Application\ClientMetier;
use Application\InterfaceClientMetier;
// the classes in PHPUnit
use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\DataProvider;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

// Testing the client layer [métier]: the server must be running
final class ClientMetierTest extends TestCase
{
     // the client's root directory
    private const string ROOT_DIRECTORY = __DIR__ . "/..";
     // client configuration
    private static array $config;
     // [métier] layer tested
    private InterfaceClientMetier $métier;

     // executed once, before the first test of the class
     #[\Override]
    public static function setUpBeforeClass(): void
    {
         // fetch the client configuration
        self::$config = json_decode(file_get_contents(self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/Data/config-client.json"), true, flags: JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
         // includes the client's dependencies (the Composer loader is already loaded by PHPUnit)
        foreach (self::$config["dependencies"] as $dependency) {
            require_once self::ROOT_DIRECTORY . "/$dependency";
        }
    }

     // run before each test
     #[\Override]
    protected function setUp(): void
    {
         // creates the layers [dao] and [métier] as in the main script
        $clientDao = new ClientDao(self::$config["urlServer"], self::$config["user"], self::$config["httpClientOptions"]);
        $this->métier = new ClientMetier($clientDao);
    }

Comments

  • lines 29–37: definition of the test environment. We use the same one as in the main script [MainImpotsClient.php];
  • Lines 41–45: Creation of the layers [dao] and [métier] before each test. The attribute [$this->métier] references the layer [métier];
  • The rest of the test, not reproduced here, is the same as in previous versions: the 11 taxpayers from the table of official figures and the [testCalculerImpot] method. Note that the [assertSame] validation requires that the values returned by the server have exactly the expected types: integers for tax, surcharge, discount, and reduction; a real number for the rate. This is ensured by the server’s [JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION] option.

This test checks the client, but also, through it, the server: the Apache server and the SGBD MySQL must be running. The test results are as follows:
